ChristianQuestions.com/youtube. 
It is one thing to fill a 
need; it is another 
thing to make 
someone needy.  God 
is not making my life 
easier by taking on my 
responsibility; He is 
helping me manage 
my responsibilities. 

What about how we look?  Will God’s care provide us  
with the best clothing at reasonable prices? 
When you think about it, outward appearance is not nearly as fundamental as 
food and shelter, and yet we often fuss over it just as much or more.  It is 
interesting that Jesus, in these verses, walks us through the more important 
matters of survival first and then addresses this one. 
My wallet is like an onion - opening it makes me cry. ― Anonymous 

Do not worry about the status of your appearance, for you can now clearly 
see that your very being is clothed with spiritual beauty: 
Matthew 6:28-30: (NASB) 28And why are you worried about clothing? Observe how the lilies 
of the field grow; they do not toil nor do they spin, 29yet I say to you that not even Solomon in 
all his glory clothed himself like one of these. 30But if God so clothes the grass of the field, 
which is alive today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace, will He not much more clothe 
you? You of little faith!  
Being called by God through Christ gives us inherent beauty.  For a Christian, it 
is the simple beauty of following Jesus that adorns us.  This does not mean we 
go to sleep having made no provisions for tomorrow’s food, or that we should 
expect clothes to grow on our backs like feathers.  Romans 12:11 tells us to not 
be slothful in business.  Romans 12:17 tells us to provide things honest in the 
sight of all men.  1 Timothy 5:8 says we are to provide for our own.  We are to 
make reasonable provisions for what we need.  
If we are dressed too richly or too poorly, both could be a distraction.  We 
 need to be godly in our dress.   
Stuff, Inner Simplicity 
• 
Getting rid of stuff in our lives and moving toward a simple life is not about 
deprivation.  It’s about getting rid of the things that don’t contribute to the 
fullness of our lives.  After all, living fully does not mean having it all, going 
everywhere, doing everything, and being all things to all people.  Many of us 
are beginning to see that too much really is too much.  Doing too much and 
having too much get in the way of being able to enjoy the things we do want 
in our lives, and to simply be who we are.  Choose intelligently the things that 
are meaningful in your life.  It may mean doing fewer things and having less 
stuff.  
Christian Fiscal ATTITUDE:  When faith is required, be faithful to it even if it 
does not look glamorous.  Accept the contributions of others to support your 
work even if it does not suit your preferences. 
Whether we are out in front in a position to be admired or if we are somewhere 
never noticed, our opportunities are all the same in God’s eyes.  We cannot 
compare with others (although we sure like to!).  We cannot judge others if 
they do not talk, act or dress like us.  Comparison causes disunity – it pulls us 
apart because we “assume” what someone is thinking or that we understand 
 their past experiences. 

Assuming gets us into all kinds of trouble.  Comparing ourselves to others is not 
within our jurisdiction.  It is not seeing with the clarity of the light that Jesus 
referred to in Matthew 6:22-23. 
Be content to accept less-than-the-greatest conditions in the Lord’s service: 
Luke 10:1-8: (NASB) 1Now after this the Lord appointed seventy others, and sent them in 
pairs ahead of him to every city and place where he himself was going to come. 2And he was 
saying to them, The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few; therefore beseech the Lord 
of the harvest to send out laborers into his harvest. 
Jesus sends out the seventy and gives us a picture of what his followers will be 
doing during the Gospel Age.  His directive was for them to go out and prepare 
the way for him in these various cities.   
You would think that this would be a big production – the warm-up act for 
Jesus in a spectacular way!  But it was not about appearance:   
3Go; behold, I send you out as lambs in the midst of wolves. 4Carry no money belt, no bag, no 
shoes; and greet no one on the way. 5Whatever house you enter, first say, Peace be to this 
house. 6If a man of peace is there, your peace will rest on him; but if not, it will return to you. 
7Stay in that house, eating and drinking what they give you; for the laborer is worthy of his 
wages. Do not keep moving from house to house. 8Whatever city you enter and they receive you, 
eat what is set before you;  
Jesus tells them to go in great humility.  He says, the laborer is worthy of his 
wages.  If someone is willing to feed you and give you a place to sleep, accept 
it.  Whatever it is they feed you, eat.  Do not go from house to house looking 
for something better – accept what God has provided.  This is powerful.  
Contributing to the greatest cause of all time is humble, simple and demanding 
work.  We have to put things in the proper order.  Not worrying about the 
outward appearance comes down to a humble approach. 

We should not need to be flashy in order to impress.  We should be godly 
and humble, letting the Lord’s word do the impressing: 
 Philippians 4:5: (KJV)  Let your moderation be known unto all men. The Lord is at hand.  
Let your moderation be known – How do you see things?  This comes back to 
having a clear spiritual eye with godly light.  If our eyes are not clear, we wash 
them out with a saline solution.  What is a saline solution?  Salt and water.  In 
Scripture, water represents truth.  Salt represents character.  Good character 
and truth are what give us the eyes to see clearly.  We see one God, we see 
Him hold our experiences, we see Him hold our times and we see Him direct 
our experiences to bring out our spiritual beauty.   

They say money doesn't bring happiness, but everyone still wants to prove it for 
themselves. ― Anonymous  

Do not worry, as we can now clearly see that God’s 
hand resides over all of our physical earthly needs: 
Matthew 6:31-32: (NASB) 31Do not worry then, saying, What will 
we eat? or What will we drink? or What will we wear for clothing? 32For 
the Gentiles eagerly seek all these things; for your heavenly Father 
knows that you need all these things.  
Everybody has these same questions and these same concerns - What will we 
eat?  What will we drink?  What do I wear? How do I look?  How do I come 
across?  Our Heavenly Father knows this.  We are in His hand – that is enough.  
Spiritually-clear sight means we see all of life from a different and higher 
perspective because we are held in the hand of God. 
Christian Fiscal ATTITUDE:  Do NOT be attached to wealth at the expense of 
following what Jesus would require of you.  
The rich young ruler came to Jesus seeking eternal life.  He was sincere 
about following the Law, and Jesus showed him a further step: 
Luke 18:21-25: (NASB) 21And he said, All these things I have kept from my youth. 22When 
Jesus heard this, he said to him, One thing you still lack; sell all that you possess and distribute 
it to the poor, and you shall have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me. 23But when he had 
heard these things, he became very sad, for he was extremely rich. 24And Jesus looked at him 
and said, How hard it is for those who are wealthy to enter the kingdom of God! 25For it is easier 
for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God. 
Let’s compare several different scriptural stories that seem to conflict with 
each other.  Which one shows us what we should be doing?   
These are not specific financial plans for us to follow.  Each story has a 
different lesson: 
The Parable of the Rich Man (Luke 12:13-21) says the landowner is a fool 
for hoarding wealth and building bigger barns.  This is a parable about 
perspective.  He sits back and thinks only about himself and how his 
wealth will grow.  Our lives should not be about our possessions. 
The story of the Rich Young Ruler (Matthew 19:16-24, Mark 10:17-25,  
Luke 18:18-22) says the rich young man cannot achieve eternal life until 
he sells ALL his possessions.  This is also about perspective.  He obeyed 
while all was comfortable, but would he continue to follow Jesus when 
all was gone?  This is what Jesus was asking him. 

In the story of Zacchaeus (Luke 19:1-10), Zacchaeus gets praised for 
giving away HALF his possessions. He is praised for his generosity and 
true repentance.  He says he will restore the money fourfold if he 
cheated anyone because he was wrong.  That was a generous thing to do 
to show his heart was in the right place. 

The Rich Religious Rulers (Mark 12:41-44) get criticized for giving large 
sums of money out of their abundance.  They walked up to the donation 
box with bells on so that others would notice the large sums they put in.  
The lesson here was that it was easy to give out of their abundance of 
wealth.  Even though they gave substantial gifts to the Temple, it did 
not cost them much since they were so wealthy. 

In contrast, The Widow’s Mite (also Mark 12:41-44) is a story about a 
poor widow who quietly scuttles up to the box and gives away ALL she 
has (two coins – a mere mite) and she has pretty much nothing.  This 
money was all she had to spend, and she gave it to the Lord’s Temple.  
Jesus points her out to his disciples in comparison to the Pharisees from 
above. 

All these are lessons of perspective.  We study them to learn the lessons about 
how our attitude should be in each situation.  We use these and apply them in 
our lives. 

It all seems to come down to what we are attached to.  Spiritual attachments 
bring earthly detachments. 
What is the final bottom line?  How should our experiences 
with money impact our walk with Jesus? 
Whether we are talking about character, jealousy, pride, relationships, 
business or money, the bottom line is always the same.  We continually need to 
check and recheck our deepest priorities and ensure that we are not veering 
off course back to earthly thinking and ways.  We have to stay with the clear 
eyes of spiritual thinking, the clear light that comes from above, rather than 
light that comes from another source that happens to be more convenient. 
Sometimes I just want someone to hug me and say, "I know it's hard, but you'll be okay. 
Here's a coffee and a million dollars.” ― Anonymous 
God gives us our experiences for specific reasons, developing us spiritually so 
that we can help others.  How are we doing with where we are? 

Because God has all aspects of your life in His hand, we 
can now freely focus on that which is MOST important –  
                                 seeking God’s kingdom. 
Jesus has brought us to this step.  Have the light of God in your eye, lighting 
your way.  Make sure the first thing you see is that there is only one God.  Make 
sure your experiences are being handled appropriately.  Make sure your time is 
in God’s hands.  Make sure your spiritual beauty is the beauty you are worried 
about.  Make sure your days and all of your experiences are in the palm of 
 God’s hand.   
Treasures in heaven are eternal; treasures on earth are temporary: 
Matthew 6:33-34: (NASB) 33But seek first His kingdom and His righteousness, and all these 
things will be added to you. 34So do not worry about tomorrow; for tomorrow will care for itself. 
Each day has enough trouble of its own.   
Does God say we will be wealthy?  No, He is talking about the necessities of 
life.  Recognize  the most important thing and do everything with that most 
important thing in mind. 
Jesus gave us these seven steps.  The first six cleared all these worries out of 
the way.  Now we can concentrate on the true treasure, being a part of God’s 
kingdom. 
This is a really important Scripture to meditate upon when we are feeling 
anxious:  Do not worry about tomorrow because tomorrow will take care of 
itself.  Make an honest assessment of what needs to be done today and do it.  
We do not worry about what is out of our control because we know it is 
completely under God’s control. 
Think about Cornelius, the first Gentile convert.   
For more on the amazing story of Cornelius, please see Episodes #866 and 870:  
“Why Cornelius – Why a Soldier?” Parts I and II. 
How did he seek God’s kingdom first?  He was a soldier of Rome.  How could he 
be a Christian?  God called him, so obviously he was able to be faithful.  He did 
not have to leave his service to Rome.  He could be faithful in the place where 
God called him.  Seek first the kingdom… Cornelius’ spirituality was 
magnificent.  He would follow along with the Jewish Law long before Peter 
ever came to see him.  He wanted to serve God; he just did not know how.  
Then Peter shows up and God’s spirit is given to Cornelius and his household, 
and he became a faithful servant.  When God calls us, He knows who we are.  
He knows where we are weak, and yet He can use us anyway. 

Christian Fiscal RESPONSIBILITY:  Exhibit generosity and understanding 
towards others above the demands of justice.   
This perspective will dictate how we receive from our Father: 
Luke 6:30-38: (NASB) 30Give to everyone who asks of you, and whoever takes away what is 
yours, do not demand it back. 31Treat others the same way you want them to treat you. 32If you 
love those who love you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners love those who love them. 
33If you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners do the 
same. 34If you lend to those from whom you expect to receive, what credit is that to you? Even 
sinners lend to sinners in order to receive back the same amount.  
Does this mean we should lend without expecting payment back?  No, but have 
generosity and understanding beyond what would be expected in a normal 
situation.  There may be times when there are circumstances, or where the 
person has a lack of maturity, and he/she will not be able to pay us back.  
Jesus is saying:  It is only money.  If we are trying to help someone and build 
them up and we give (time or money) and it is not reciprocated, it is okay.  We 
did what we thought was the right thing to do.   
If we remember this Scripture, if the person needs help, we should be satisfied 
with our part even if we are never repaid.  We need to rise above what 
everyone else expects, not giving out money foolishly, but with generosity 
when needed.  
35But love your enemies, and do good, and lend, expecting nothing in return; and your reward 
will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High; for He Himself is kind to ungrateful and 
evil men. 36Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful. 37Do not judge, and you will not be 
judged; and do not condemn, and you will not be condemned; pardon, and you will be pardoned. 
38Give, and it will be given to you. They will pour into your lap a good measure—pressed down, 
shaken together, and running over. For by your standard of measure it will be measured to you 
in return. 
We need to be magnanimous with our money, in our attitude of how we treat 
others.  Jesus is not separating out our dollars and cents from our integrity in 
dealing with our enemies.  He is mixing it all together because this same 
principle applies to everything.  We should have the same magnanimous 
attitude Jesus did.  He loved his enemies.  He died for his enemies.  He died 
for those who took him captive.  He even healed the ear of one of the men who 
arrested him.   

All interactions with friends, neighbors and 
even enemies are opportunities to let our light 
shine.  People pay particular attention when we 
are generous and merciful with money, 
especially if done in a humble way.  We should 
act in a godly fashion, letting our actions speak 
as a witness to God.  You will never go wrong 
by being overly generous.  
All of these Seven Steps to Heavenly Treasure are encouraging us to be 
unattached to earthly wealth and especially to the desire for it: 
1 Timothy 6:6-10: (NASB) 6But godliness actually is a means of great gain when accompanied 
by contentment. 7For we have brought nothing into the world, so we cannot take anything out 
of it either. 8If we have food and covering, with these we shall be content. 9But those who want 
to get rich fall into temptation and a snare and many foolish and harmful desires which plunge 
men into ruin and destruction. 10For the love of money is a root of all sorts of evil, and some by 
longing for it have wandered away from the faith and pierced themselves with many griefs. 
Godliness with contentment is great gain.  We live in a culture where wanting 
to be rich is normal.  That constant longing for a wealthy lifestyle contradicts 
our longing to follow Jesus.  We do not need to “keep up with the 
Kardashians!”  This can be very dangerous.  

There is nothing wrong with having, but there is something wrong if what we 
have rules over our lives instead of us using it as a tool to serve God. 
We did not talk about the investing in the Parables of the Pounds and Talents 
or the business dealings regarding Vineyards and Stewards.  We did not address 
the forgiving of impossible debts or the lessons Jesus taught the Pharisees 
about fiscal perspective or much about the Widow’s Mite.  Jesus said a lot 
more about money, but these are lessons for another day. 
We have been given a privilege to live in this time.  Right now things might be 
a little difficult, but think about the abundance the vast majority of us have in 
relation to people in the past.  We are truly blessed.  How clear is my eye with 
spiritual light to see that I need to serve God with this blessing?  Even if my 
contribution is small, I can still have an incredible impact by using what I have 
been given for the good of someone else and to the glory of God.   

So, what did Jesus teach us about money? 
For Jonathan and Rick (and Julie) and Christian Questions... 

Did God Make Heaven and Hell Humanity’s Destiny? (Part I) 
Matthew 6:10: (NASB) Your kingdom come. Your will be done, 
 on earth as it is in heaven.  
The general consensus in Christianity is that there are two 
paths - two destinies that await humanity.  First, there is the 
heavenly bliss of being with Jesus.  After all, Jesus himself said 
he was preparing a place for his followers in heaven, and he 
also said he would bring us there.  Second, there is the fiery, 
torturous eternal existence of hell.  This is reserved for 
everyone else who did not follow Jesus.  While this “two-
destiny” approach may sound simple, it does not stand the test 
of scrutiny.  For starters, the fact is that the vast majority of 
humanity has not known or accepted the name of Jesus.  Does this mean that 
God’s careful creation of humanity “in His image” was a resounding failure?  And 
what about planet earth?  If it is doomed for a fiery end, then why did Jesus tell 
us to pray for God’s kingdom to come on earth?   These are just the beginning of 
some big questions, so let’s see if we can find big, biblical answers. 
Many Christians envision the afterlife as a binary concept of either heaven or 
hell.  There are several factors we need to put in place to reveal God’s 
ultimate plan for all humanity.   

Let’s begin with the earth.  The Apostle Peter paints a dramatic picture of the 
earth’s destiny. 
He begins by fast forwarding to conditions of the last days: 
2 Peter 3:3-4: (NASB) 3Know this first of all, that in the last days mockers will come with 
their mocking, following after their own lusts, 4and saying, Where is the promise of his coming? 
For ever since the fathers fell asleep, all continues just as it was from the beginning of creation.  
Ancient prophesies being mocked by self-centered people.  This sounds 
familiar, as we are now in the last days. 

Peter next reviews an ancient judgment that reminds us of God’s ultimate 
control: 
2 Peter 3:5-8: (NASB) 5For when they maintain this, it escapes their notice that by the word 
of God the heavens existed long ago and the earth was formed out of water and by water, 
6through which the world at that time was destroyed, being flooded with water. 
What was destroyed?  The previous heavens and earth. 
We suggest this is a symbolic destruction.  The heavens represent the spiritual 
and governmental ways of the world that existed before the Flood, and the 
earth represents humanity’s social order.  
This tells us the “world” that was destroyed consisted of the heavens and the 
earth.  The King James Version of verse 6 calls this the world that was.  The 
world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished.  We know the 
actual ball of earth and the sky were not literally destroyed.  
Next comes the destiny of the present heavens and earth: 
7But by His word the present heavens and earth are being reserved for fire, kept for the day of 
judgment and destruction of ungodly men. 8But do not let this one fact escape your notice, 
beloved, that with the Lord one day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years like one day.  
The day of judgment is not a single 24-hour day. Like the Flood, will weed out 
unrighteousness.  

The present heavens and earth, meaning this present evil world we live in now 
is reserved for fire - that sounds pretty scary – there is fire and destruction, 
and it sounds like it will last a really long time!  What does this mean? 
This verse has a lot of symbolism which we will prove as we continue. 
It says this day of judgment is like a thousand years - it is not a day of 
reprimand and destruction.  It is a day of judgment - a day of trial.  The Greek 
word for judgment, krisis, actually means “trial.”  While this might sound 
scary, a more detailed study shows it is a necessary time of repentance and 
learning.  Judgment is ultimately for the purpose of reconciling man back to 
God.  Man will have the opportunity to learn righteousness (many for the very 
first time), make amends and move forward in the kingdom.   
Peter now reminds us of God’s desire for life and his judgment upon sin: 
2 Peter 3:9-13: (NASB) 9The Lord is not slow about His promise, as some count slowness, but 
is patient toward you, not wishing (“not minded”) for any to perish but for all to come to 
repentance. 10But the day of the Lord will come like a thief, in which the heavens will pass away 
with a roar and the elements will be destroyed with intense heat, and the earth and its works 
will be burned up.  

Not wishing for any to perish - the word wishing is a poor translation.  It means 
“not minded,” or “not of the mind.”  God did not have in His mind for any to 
perish.  Instead, He wanted an opportunity for repentance.  In order for the 
repentance to happen, the present social order needs to be removed.  That is 
where this picture of the intense heat and the “destruction” of the earth 
comes in.  It is the destruction of the social order because that is where the 
problem stems.  It must be removed in order to be replaced with something 
productive.  It is NOT in God's mind to torment and torture. 
We believe this to be symbolic heat and burning, showing the complete 
destruction of the way the world is run by the social and false religious systems 
of this present world.  We know the destruction is symbolic because we already 
have scriptural precedent that tells us the first heavens and earth, the world 
that was, was “destroyed.”  Now the world that is will also be “destroyed.” 
The day of judgment is a time of learning and repentance.  Understanding this 
takes the fear out of serving God – He is not condemning the majority of 
mankind to eternal torment.  The day of judgment is hopeful for humanity.   

What should this mean for those who follow Jesus: 
11Since all these things are to be destroyed <3089> in this way, what sort of people ought you 
to be in holy conduct and godliness, 12looking for and hastening the coming of the day of God, 
because of which the heavens will be destroyed by burning, and the elements will melt with 
intense heat! 13But according to His promise we are looking for new <2357> heavens and a new 
earth, in which righteousness dwells.  

Destroyed:  Strongs #3089 luo; a primary verb; to "loosen"  
 King James Version translates this as:  break (up), destroy, dissolve, (un-) loose, melt, put off 
When something is destroyed or loosened, it is pulled off; it is pulled away 
from its moorings and it is not recoverable.  This is what happens to the 
present social order - the present evil world.  It is put out of commission.  
New:  Strongs #2537 kainos; new (especially in freshness) 
It is a renewed earth, not a brand-new earth, just like the renewed earth and 
social order after the great Flood.  

How can we be sure the earth will not be literally destroyed?   
Is there other scriptural proof? 

One of the amazing things about the Bible is that 
throughout all of its books it verifies the truths that it 
teaches.  There is great power and confirmation that one 
writer living in a specific time agrees with other writers 
living at different times and places.  Let’s look at seven different Old 
Testament Bible writers who all agree on the future destiny of the earth.   
Zephaniah starts out seeming to prove the earth WILL be destroyed: 
Zephaniah 3:8-11: (NASB) 8Therefore wait for Me, declares the LORD, for the day when I 
rise up as a witness. Indeed, My decision is to gather nations, to assemble kingdoms, to pour out 
on them My indignation, all My burning anger; for all the earth will be devoured by the fire of 
My zeal.  
The book of Zephaniah has both literal and prophetic warnings that happened 
in the Old Testament.  There was a judgment against the nation of Judah back 
then, but this gathering of all nations and the pouring out of indignations on 
them was never literally fulfilled - so it is yet future.  This refers to a coming 
global day of judgment. 
What happens as a result of this fiery devouring?  Does the earth 
become crispy and useless?  Did the fire burn it out and take all of 
the goodness and all of the life right out of it?  
Let’s look at the next verse for the answer:  
9For then I will give to the peoples purified lips, that all of them may call on the 
name of the LORD, to serve Him shoulder to shoulder.  
If the earth was burned, where are these people who still have lips calling on 
the name of the Lord?  This is a conversion of the nations who have been 
gathered to serve God.  Are they in heaven?  
Where is this purification taking place AFTER the earth is devoured by God’s 
anger? 
10From beyond the rivers of Ethiopia My worshipers, My dispersed ones, will bring My offerings. 
11In that day you will feel no shame because of all your deeds by which you have rebelled against 
Me; for then I will remove from your midst your proud, exulting ones, and you will never again 
be haughty on My holy mountain.  
The answer:  it is on earth!  It talks about from beyond the rivers of Ethiopia –
there is no Ethiopia in heaven.  The idea is, even though Zephaniah says the 
earth will be devoured by the fire of My zeal, we also have the assurance that 
earth was not to be destroyed.  Zephaniah gives us a dramatic view of earth's 
destiny.   
Let's go through several other Old Testament writers and look at what they say 
about the destiny of earth.  Does the earth abide forever or is the earth meant 
for destruction?  We have two very dramatically different potential end results.  
What do the Scriptures say?  

Moses gives us the earliest view of God’s clear intentions for the earth.  This 
statement takes place right after the flood: 
Genesis 8:20-22: (NASB) 20Then Noah built an altar to the LORD, and took of every clean 
animal and of every clean bird and offered burnt offerings on the altar. 21The LORD smelled the 
soothing aroma; and the LORD said to Himself, I will never again curse the ground on account 
of man, for the intent of man's heart is evil from his youth; and I will never again destroy every 
living thing, as I have done. 22While the earth remains, seedtime and harvest, and cold and heat, 
and summer and winter, and day and night shall not cease.  
Technically it says WHILE the earth remains, so there is a thought of repetition 
and continuance, but also conditional - as long as the earth is still here.  On its 
own, this text does not prove the earth remains forever, but that is why a 
topical Bible study is important to bring in supporting Scriptures. 
This verse does prove that God said, I will never again destroy every living 
thing, as I have done.  Peter described the worldwide destruction of heaven 
and earth that had taken place and God promises not to do that again.  If we 
say the earth is going to be burned up with fire, God would be contradicting 
Himself, and we know He cannot.  We have the affirmative statement that He 
will never again destroy every living thing. 
Now we have a specific statement by Solomon defining God’s plan of 
perpetuity for earth: 
Ecclesiastes 1:3-4: (NASB) 3What advantage does man have in all his work which he does 
under the sun? 4A generation goes and a generation comes, but the earth remains forever 
<5769>.  
Forever:  Strongs #5769 owlam; or olam; properly, concealed, i.e., the vanishing point; 
generally, time out of mind (past or future), i.e. (practically) eternity  
The idea of the vanishing point is a great 
definition.  When we look at the horizon 
for miles, at some point it looks like the 
world ends but there is still more 
horizon.  It is beyond the vanishing point.  
The next verse is going to add on to 
<5769>.  Solomon says the earth abides or 
remains forever, over and beyond the 
vanishing point.   
David brings unmistakable emphasis to the perpetuity of the earth: 
Psalm 104:5: (NASB) He established the earth upon its foundations, so that it will not totter 
forever <5769 and ever <5703>.  
Ever:  Strongs #5703 `ad; duration, in the sense of advance or perpetuity  
This builds on the Ecclesiastes text.  It is a perpetual, self-fulfilling movement 
forward that does not ever stop.  If we throw something in outer space it will 
just keep going because there is nothing to stop it; there is no gravity.  That is 
the sense of the earth.  It is being described as a planet of perpetuity. 
The Bible unequivocally tells us the earth is not burned up.  

Isaiah adds an unmistakable reason for God’s clearly-stated plan for the 
perpetuity of the earth: 
Isaiah 45:18: (NASB) For thus says the LORD, who created the heavens (He is the God who 
formed the earth and made it, He established it and did not create it a waste place, but formed 
it to be inhabited), I am the LORD, and there is none else.  
In one sense, we could say it has never been thoroughly inhabited.  Only 29.1 
percent of the earth is land; the rest is ocean.  Of that, only about 71 percent 
is habitable.  The rest – which is about 27 million square miles – is glaciers and 
barren land like deserts, beaches and exposed rocks.  Of the inhabited land, 
one percent is built-up urban areas including cities, towns, villages, roads and 
other human infrastructure.  There is a lot of room around here that needs to 
be rebalanced, but it is not thoroughly inhabitable. 

The LORD formed the world to be inhabited.  Does this mean it is inhabited by 
 human beings forever?   
We are going through different books of the Old Testament so we can see 
plainly that the Bible as a unit is teaching us something incredible that most of 
us miss. 
Ezekiel reinforces the perpetuity of the earth and its connection to the 
future of Israel: 
Ezekiel 37:24-28: (NASB) 24My servant David (this is a picture of Christ – Jesus was born from 
the house of David) will be king over them, and they will all have one shepherd; and they will 
walk in My ordinances and keep My statutes and observe them. 25They will live on the land that 
I gave to Jacob My servant, in which your fathers lived; and they will live on it, they, and their 
sons and their sons' sons, forever; and David My servant will be their prince forever. 26I will 
make a covenant of peace with them; it will be an everlasting covenant with them. And I will 
place them and multiply them, and will set My sanctuary in their midst forever. 27My dwelling 
place also will be with them; and I will be their God, and they will be My people. 28And the 
nations will know that I am the LORD who sanctifies Israel, when My sanctuary is in their midst 
forever. 

They will live on the land that I gave to Jacob – unmistakably this is planet 
earth.  For how long?  It says their sons and their sons’ sons forever… it will be 
an everlasting covenant (promise) with them.  God will set His sanctuary in 
their midst forever.  This is a clear picture - earth, Israel, God's promise, God’s 
sanctuary - all there forever!  Incidentally, it says, and the nations will know 
that I am the Lord who sanctifies Israel, so now there are other people in this 
picture forever on earth.   
Finally, Daniel, while interpreting a dream, reveals God’s everlasting plans 
for ALL humanity on earth: 
Daniel 2:34-35: (NASB) 34You continued looking until a stone was cut out without hands, and 
it struck the statue on its feet of iron and clay and crushed them. 35Then the iron, the clay, the 
bronze, the silver and the gold were crushed all at the same time and became like chaff from 
the summer threshing floors; and the wind carried them away so that not a trace of them was 
found. But the stone that struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the whole earth. 
In this symbolic dream, the stone destroys the statue, grinds it to dust, the 
wind blows it away and the stone becomes a great mountain and fills the 
earth.  
Daniel 2:44-45: (NASB) 44In the days of those kings the God of heaven will set up a kingdom 
which will never be destroyed, and that kingdom will not be left for another people; it will 
crush and put an end to all these kingdoms, but it will itself endure forever. 45Inasmuch as you 
saw that a stone was cut out of the mountain without hands and that it crushed the iron, the 
bronze, the clay, the silver and the gold, the great God has made known to the king what will 
take place in the future; so the dream is true and its interpretation is trustworthy. 

King Nebuchadnezzar had a dream but forgot it.  
Daniel had to tell him what the dream was, and 
then what it represented.  It was a dead-on 
prediction of the defeat of world powers in the 
correct order represented by different body 
parts of a giant statue of a man:  Babylon, 
Medo-Persian, Greece and Rome.  Eventually 
the stone cut without hands strikes the statue 
down and starts to fill the whole earth; that 
stone being God’s kingdom, a holy government.  
God’s administration is controlling the earth.  
God has it the way He designed it from the 
start. 

No matter how we look at this, there are many Scriptures that focus on various 
aspects of the everlasting nature of earth and the intentions behind it. 

The details and the variety of sources about earth’s future are convincing.  
God’s word is so inspiring! 
With the earth established as a future domain for humanity,  
should our view of heaven change? 
We define heaven as the spiritual realm outside of our earthly understanding in 
which God and His holy angels dwell.  While this realm is unfathomable to our 
simple human minds, we are given a lot to go on in terms of understanding how 
it fits in with the future of a select few who follow Christ. 
Until Jesus came, there was never a promise or 
expectation of a heavenly reward.  This represents 
millions of people who never heard his name. 
We are not minimizing heaven, but do not forget the earth!  Not only does the 
earth abide forever; it has an eternal purpose for humanity. 

OPPORTUNITY 
Jesus introduced the concept of heavenly glory, though his disciples were 
not able to grasp it: 
Matthew 5:11-12: (NASB) 11Blessed are you when people insult you and persecute you, and 
falsely say all kinds of evil against you because of me. 12Rejoice and be glad, for your reward in 
heaven is great; for in the same way they persecuted the prophets who were before you. 
Your reward in heaven is great - without having an expectation of a heavenly 
reward, we wonder if those disciples listening to the Sermon on the Mount 
 were confused about what Jesus meant. 

PLACE 
Before his crucifixion, Jesus made sure his followers knew they 
were going to have a specific place with him in heaven:  
John 14:1-3: (NASB) 1Do not let your heart be troubled; believe in God, believe also in me. 
2In my Father's house are many dwelling places; if it were not so, I would have told you; for I go 
to prepare a place for you. 3If I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again and receive 
you to myself, that where I am, there you may be also.  
We all want to know what heaven is like.  Here we are told it is being 
“renovated” or a new section is being built just for the faithful followers of 
Jesus!  It does not give us a lot of information to satisfy our curiosity, but we 
do know that Jesus will be there.  Something new and unique is being 
prepared. 

COMPARATIVE VALUE   
What waits for the faithful followers of Jesus is an eternal 
existence far beyond any human experience: 
2 Corinthians 4:16-18: (NASB) 16Therefore we do not lose heart, but though our outer man 
is decaying, yet our inner man is being renewed day by day. 17For momentary, light affliction is 
producing for us an eternal weight of glory far beyond all comparison, 18while we look not at 
the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen; for the things which are seen 
are temporal, but the things which are not seen are eternal. 

Temporal vs. eternal – What we see here on earth is not what is in heaven.  
The trials of this life are producing in us an eternal weight of glory far beyond 
all comparison.  These things which are not seen are eternal. 
Trauma does not feel like momentary, light affliction, but our life here is but a 
flicker in time compared to the glory and magnificence of heaven.    

INHERITANCE 
Jesus’ disciples will share glory with Jesus: 
Romans 8:17-22: (NASB) 17and if children, heirs also, heirs of God and fellow heirs with 
Christ, if indeed we suffer with him so that we may also be glorified with him. 18For I consider 
that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory that is to 
be revealed to us.  
If indeed we suffer with him…we may also be glorified with him – this is huge!   

MISSION 
The call of heaven has everything to do with blessing the sin-sick 
world, who long for deliverance: 
19For the anxious longing of the creation waits eagerly for the revealing of the sons of God. 20For 
the creation was subjected to futility, not willingly, but because of Him who subjected it, in 
hope 21that the creation itself also will be set free from its slavery to corruption into the 
freedom of the glory of the children of God. 22For we know that the whole creation groans and 
suffers the pains of childbirth together until now.  

Two groups are described - one is being freed from slavery and the other is 
helping facilitate the release of the slaves.  The creation itself also will be set 
free from its slavery to corruption into the freedom of the glory of the 
children of God - the followers of Christ are the children of God and the 
 creation is the “everybody else.” 
Part of the mission of those who go to heaven (the followers of Christ) is the 
reconciliation of mankind (the creation) back to God.  Heaven is not a place of 
inactivity.  Heaven is working to fulfill the plan of the Almighty God. 

CLOSENESS TO GOD 
If the disciples of Jesus will be with him and he is at the right 
hand of God, they are in the most sacred position imaginable:  
Colossians 3:1-4: (NASB) 1Therefore if you have been raised up with Christ, keep seeking 
the things above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God. 2Set your mind on the things 
above, not on the things that are on earth. 3For you have died and your life is hidden with Christ 
in God. 4When Christ, who is our life, is revealed, then you also will be revealed with him in 
glory.  
Heaven is no small matter!  This is a massive privilege being offered through 
God’s grace.  There is nothing we can do to earn this – it is through the grace 
    of God and the role Jesus plays in our justification. 

THE GLORIOUS FINALITY OF HEAVEN 
Heaven will mean everlasting life:  
Revelation 2:10: (NASB) …Be faithful until death, and I will give you the crown 
of life. 
A “crowning” accomplishment of someone is their greatest success.   

TYPE OF HEAVENLY NATURE 
Not just life but life of the divine nature: 
2 Peter 1:3-4: (NASB) 3seeing that His divine power has granted to us everything pertaining 
to life and godliness, through the true knowledge of Him who called us by His own glory and 
excellence. 4For by these He has granted to us His precious and magnificent promises, so that 
by them you may become partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is 
in the world by lust. 
The divine nature is immortality.  It means life perpetuates itself from within.  
No external source is needed to sustain life.  A divine being is indestructible 
and death-proof.  God does not arbitrarily give this divine nature.  See also 
Romans 2:7 and 1 Corinthians 15:53,54.  This is the same plane of existence as 
God and Christ, and is being offered to the true followers of Jesus - only a tiny 
fraction of mankind. 

These are not just “good” people; they have sacrificed their will and life to 
become crystalized in Christlikeness so that once they are released from this 
human condition, they will not flinch away from anything in relation to God’s 
will.  The test has to be to penetrate our very core.  God must know that we 
are eternally loyal.   
This privilege is so high that He cannot take the chance of someone becoming a 
Satan.  Satan was faithful and glorified God but something happened when he 
decided he wanted to be like the Most High in Isaiah 14:14.  Satan was and is 
very powerful.  Great power will find the worst in you.  Can you imagine if 
Satan had the divine nature, if he was immortal and could not be killed? 
This upward call or high calling to be partakers of the divine 
nature is NOT to become an angel.  There is no Scripture that 
even hints that man dies and turns into an angel, sitting on a 
cloud with a harp, protecting their loved ones from on high.  This is a MUCH 
higher plane of existence than the angels. 
1 Corinthians 6:3 tells us that one 
of the responsibilities of this 
divine class will be to judge the 
angels.  The word for judge in this 
text uses the Greek word krino, meaning “to rule or govern,” so they will have 
some authority over the angels.  It is the highest position in the universe. 

The Bible gives us just a tiny glimpse of the magnificence of heaven.   
Exactly who is going to heaven?  
Is such glory and power being offered to anyone who loves Jesus? 

This does not have to be a hard question to answer.  Let’s think for a moment 
about Satan having once been a mighty, God-serving spiritual being and how his 
pride brought him down.  Do we think for one moment that God would offer 
such power to millions who were not first thoroughly tested?   
Would God offer deathlessness to us just because we like Him?  No, of course 
not.  This would be a dangerous practice.  Getting into heaven and being 
offered immortality requires serious consideration on God’s part and serious 
dedication on the believer’s part.   

A follower of Christ who wishes to get to heaven cannot just meet the 
minimum standards that allow millions to have memberships in most 
denominations of Christianity.  These standards are far below the Master's 
standards.  When given the choice of only heaven or hell, our loving natures 
want to put everyone we know and like – all the “good people” - in heaven, 
regardless of how dedicated to Christ and whether or not they have led a 
sacrificial life. 
This has come about because we have oversimplified a very profound subject.  
If there is no other choice at death but to send someone to heaven or hell, we 
are left with confusion and despair.   

How do we get to heaven?   
WHAT DOES THE CALL LOOK LIKE? 
The only way to receive an offer of discipleship is to be called by God and 
to accept that call: 
John 6:44: (NASB) No one can come to me unless the Father who sent me draws him; and I 
will raise him up on the last day. 
Remember we talked about all the millions of 
people who died before Christ, who never 
even heard his name?  There are billions of 
people living since the time of Jesus who have heard of him, but whom the 
Father has never called.  There is no scriptural loophole to get them into 
heaven - this includes many we would call “good” people.  Where do they go?  
We talked earlier about the earth abiding forever and people being on that 
earth for a reason!  Plus, we are only using a small fraction of the earth for the 
current residents.  These people will have a home on this earth.  We will 
address this further in Part II. 
The path to follow Jesus is a difficult and rarely traveled path: 
Matthew 7:13-14: (NASB) 13Enter through the narrow gate; for the gate is wide and the way 
is broad that leads to destruction, and there are many who enter through it. 14For the gate is 
small and the way is narrow that leads to life, and there are few who find it.  

There is a narrow gate and a narrow way that leads to life, only a few find it.  
Then there is a broad way that leads to destruction (not eternal torture).   
We will address this further in Part II.  But the point here is that following 
Jesus is a difficult road.  How do we know?  We have only to look at the life of 
Jesus.  It was not easy, and to be a “footstep follower” of Jesus means we are 
walking right behind him, doing what he did.  He lived a difficult life of 
sacrifice. 

Following Jesus means walking in his footsteps.  This means we must be 
willing to be selfless: 
Luke 9:23-24: (NASB) 23And he was saying to them all, If anyone wishes to come after me, 
he must deny himself, and take up his cross daily and follow me. 24For whoever wishes to save 
his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for my sake, he is the one who will save it. 
We are to “die daily” for Christ (1 Corinthians 15:31).  Are we willing to give up 
our lives, to lose ourselves in doing the will of God?  Because it is so difficult, 
we need to consider the following: 
It is expected that we think through such a decision with great care: 
Luke 14:27-28: (NASB) 27Whoever does not carry his own cross and come after me cannot be 
my disciple.28For which one of you, when he wants to build a tower, does not first sit down and 
calculate the cost to see if he has enough to complete it? 
This calling goes beyond just loving Jesus or accepting him as your personal 
savior.  It is the difference between being a fan of Jesus and being a disciple of 
Jesus.  

It is wonderful to love Jesus and accept him as our personal savior.  But to go 
further, to be a true disciple, we need to accept the necessity of giving up 
everything for the sake of Christ.  Are we willing to walk in his footsteps and 
live our lives with the selfless mindset he exhibited?  To do the will of God 
always instead of our own despite whatever trial or tribulation might come?  
THIS is the difference between a fan and a disciple.   
We talked about what going to heaven encompasses, how massive this reward 
is and the great importance of the responsibilities of those who seek and 
accept it.  God does not give such a reward lightly.  That is why the Scriptures 
give us all these things to understand the extent of true discipleship. 

WHAT ARE THE DAILY EXPERIENCES OF THOSE CALLED TO FOLLOW 
JESUS, WHO RECEIVE A HEAVENLY REWARD? 
God’s will: A disciple of Jesus always focuses on sacrificing their own will for 
Romans 12:1-2: (NASB) 1Therefore I urge you, brethren, by the mercies of God, to present 
your bodies a living and holy sacrifice, acceptable to God, which is your spiritual service of 
worship. 2And do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your 
mind, so that you may prove what the will of God is, that which is good and acceptable and 
perfect.  
This is an invitation, not a command, or else it 
would not be a sacrifice. The Lord’s people 
are not commanded to present their bodies a 
living and holy sacrifice, or walk in the footsteps of Jesus or take up their cross 
daily and follow him.  They are urged to do so.  Voluntary service to God is a 
privilege and an opportunity.  It is only by grace this option is available.   
If we are called, it is our Father’s will that we accept His grace, and His will is 
good and acceptable and perfect.  We may be invited to this life, but we do 
not have to accept it.  Though it is a great privilege, if we accept, we agree to 
follow we agree to follow the guidelines laid out for us.  We want to live our 
lives according to the privilege of sacrifice.  Romans 12:1-2 talks about 
transforming ourselves by the renewing of our mind through the holy spirit 
(God’s power and influence) working within us. 

A disciple of Jesus is not exempt from sin, but they do need to ask 
forgiveness for their sins: 
1 John 2:1-2: (NASB) 1My little children, I am writing these things to you so that you may 
not sin. And if anyone sins, we have an Advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous; 
2and he himself is the propitiation for our sins; and not for ours only, but also for those of the 
whole world.  
Even the most faithful Christians are still sinful human beings.  They are able, 
however, to bring their sins to the throne of grace through Jesus, since he is 
the satisfaction for those sins.  We must recognize our sins and be deeply 
repentant.  It is not enough to say, I am sorry.  We must live repentant lives for 
those sins, seeking to undo their damage if at all possible.  This is required.    

For a disciple of Jesus, the most important goal in life is their faithfulness: 
Philippians 3:12-14: (NASB) 12Not that I have already obtained it or have already become 
perfect, but I press on so that I may lay hold of that for which also I was laid hold of by Christ 
Jesus. 13Brethren, I do not regard myself as having laid hold of it yet; but one thing I do: 
forgetting what lies behind and reaching forward to what lies ahead, 14I press on toward the 
goal for the prize of the upward call of God in Christ Jesus. 
The prize of the upward call of God in the King James Version reads the prize 
of the high calling.  If Jesus learned obedience by the things he suffered, as 
we are told in Hebrews 5:8, we should also.   
Tricia asks:  If we have to give up everything to follow Christ, should we not 
work, have a home or a family? 
No, we know from Colossians 3:17 (and others) that whatsoever ye do in word 
or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus.  We are representatives of Jesus 
and the Father.  We offer our livelihood to God; this is our service and our 
sacrifice.  We use whatever we have to serve Him and His cause.  
Our homes are in His service, our children are taught His ways and His plans.  
The New Testament is full of those individuals who supported others like the 
Apostle Paul, who gave up all to serve spreading the gospel message.   
The call for each of us is unique.  The Apostle Paul was called to be an apostle.  
He stayed in the homes of other Christians.  His work, like his life, was 
financed by other Christians who worked in the world in order to do that.   
Even Paul worked sporadically to support himself with tent making.  Each 
disciple is a steward, a caretaker of this life and all we have given to God.   
We have this high calling – this goal of being faithful in our lives, and we are to 
use whatever the Father has given us to accomplish this. 
A disciple of Jesus will be tried and tested to show their fidelity to Christ: 
1 Peter 4:12-14: (NASB) 12Beloved, do not be surprised at the fiery ordeal among you, which 
comes upon you for your testing, as though some strange thing were happening to you; 13but to 
the degree that you share the sufferings of Christ, keep on rejoicing, so that also at the 
revelation of his glory you may rejoice with exultation. 14If you are reviled for the name of 
Christ, you are blessed, because the Spirit of glory and of God rests on you.  
The whole world is not on trial for eternal life 
at this time.  It is only those who have been 
called of God and are running for that prize of 
the high calling.  The rest of humanity are not “lost” if they do not accept 
Jesus now in this lifetime.  This is where so many Christians become confused 
about what happens to all those people who are “good” but not “good enough” 
to be part of this very difficult high calling.  We will address this in more detail 
next week in Part II.   
What does it take to get to heaven?  A lot!  It takes everything we 
have.  The fiery ordeal in the text above is for our purification.  Fire 
can destroy, but it is also used to burn off the impurities in precious 
metals.  We are being purified by our difficult experiences. 

A disciple of Jesus understands their training now is for a higher purpose 
later: 
2 Corinthians 5:18-20: (WEY) 18And all this is from God, who has reconciled us to Himself 
through Christ, and has appointed us to serve in the ministry of reconciliation. 19We are to tell 
how God was in Christ reconciling the world to Himself, not charging men's transgressions to 
their account, and that He has entrusted to us the Message of this reconciliation. 20…we, on 
Christ's behalf, beseech men to be reconciled to God.   
God has a plan to reconcile the world, not just Christians, but the entire world 
to Himself.  All those who are not on trial in the present time will eventually 
need to be reconciled to God.  Faithful Christians are being trained now for 
that higher purpose, for that future ministry. 
A disciple of Jesus is focused on the future, both for themselves and for the 
world they will serve: 
1 Peter 2:12: (NASB) Keep your behavior excellent among the Gentiles, so that in the thing 
in which they slander you as evildoers, they may because of your good deeds, as they observe 
them, glorify God in the day of visitation. 
What is the day of visitation?  It is the day of judgment, the time that period 
begins the process of ALL THINGS being made right with God.  A disciple of 
Jesus is focused on this future.  The example the disciples of Jesus give now 
with their sacrificial lives will be evident in that day of visitation.  Those who 
despise these faithful ones now will realize that they have been a good 
reflection of the will of God.  Such lives will be an example of good deeds.  
Notice that these Gentiles, or people who are not godly in their lives now, are 
glorifying God in this verse.  People in a burning hell of torment are not 
glorifying God.  There must be someplace else God has in store for them rather 
than condemning them to hell.

Are We Living in the “End Times”? 
Daniel 12:1: (ASV) …and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was 
since there was a nation even to that same time:… 
Special Guest:  David Stein 
People believe in the Bible to varying degrees.  Some of us see 
it as the unerring word of God, while others see it as an account 
of history, wisdom and standards.  Still others see it as sprinkled 
with both wisdom and folly. Then we have those who see no 
value in it at all.  For the most part, one of the common threads 
that all who know something about the Bible seem to share is 
the belief that it speaks of God’s wrath and apocalyptic events.  
While these are true perceptions of the Bible, they are by no 
means a complete picture.  How can we know what the “End 
Times” are and when they start?  What kinds of things happen 
during these times? Is there any tangible proof of the End Times that can 
establish the credibility of Bible prophecy to the skeptic?  Where do we start?  
David, our friend and brother-in-Christ, has been on 
Christian Questions several times before.  Most recently 
he guided us on our series called, “Has the Bible Been 
Mistranslated and Misunderstood?”  Search these 
episode numbers to hear more: 
Ep. 1151: (Part I) 
Ep. 1152: (Part II) 
Ep. 1153: (Part III) 
Ep. 1162: (Part IV) 
Ep. 1163: (Part V) 

What Scriptures refer to the time of the end? 
The phrase time of the end occurs in the Bible six times, and only in the book 
of Daniel.  Let’s examine the timing particulars of how it is used in five of the 
six uses. 
The time of the end is a specifically-appointed time: 
Daniel 8:17: (ASV) …Understand, O son of man; for the vision belongeth to the time of the 
end.  
Daniel 8:19: (ASV) And he said, Behold, I will make thee know what shall be in the latter 
time of the indignation; for it belongeth to the appointed time of the end.  
Daniel 11:35: (ASV) …even to the time of the end; because it is yet for the time appointed.  
These ideas of time are very important to us because our God is a God of time.  
Prophecy always involves time.  Here in Daniel, the phrase time of the end 
shows God is operating within a chronology.  It indicates there is an end to the 
age of sin and death, and something more wonderful is coming. 

The time of the end is the demarcation point from what is wrong with the 
world        to what is right with the world.  Daniel tells us it is a specifically-
appointed time. 
It is NOT to be understood until it is upon the world: 
Daniel 12:4: (ASV) But thou, O Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book, even to the 
time of the end:…   
Daniel 12:9: (ASV) …Go thy way, Daniel; for the words are shut up and sealed till the time 
of the end.  
Our God is a God of progressive revelation, meaning things become clearer as 
time goes on.  The prophecies in Daniel specifically have to do with the time of 
the end, but Daniel was told they will not be understood.   
Shut up the words, and seal the book - the details will not be understood until 
those who live in the time of the end read it.  They will need the prophecy to 
identify when they are living and what they are supposed to do. 

Jesus used a similar phrase in the New Testament - end of the age (or end of 
the world in the King James Version and other older translations).  He does not 
use exactly the same language or the same words, but it has much the same 
meaning.  The word for age in this case is the Greek word aion.  
Age:  Strongs #165, aiṓn; properly, an age; by extension, perpetuity (also past); by implication, 
the world; specifically (Jewish) a Messianic period (present or future): age, course, eternal,  
(for) ever(-more), (n-)ever, (beginning of the, while the) world (began, without end) 
This word refers to a period of time.  Remember, the prophecies in Daniel are 
also all about time.  Jesus gives us several more hints in the following texts.  
Christianity will be corrupted, and that corruption will be revealed at the 
end of the age: 
Matthew 13:39-40,49: (NIV) 39and the enemy who sows them is the devil. The harvest is 
the end of the age <165>, and the harvesters are angels. 40As the weeds are pulled up and 
burned in the fire, so it will be at the end of the age <165>. 49This is how it will be at the end 
of the age <165>. The angels will come and separate the wicked from the righteous. 
Jesus is saying the same thing as Daniel - there will be an end of the age.  He 
gives us a particular feature of this time by talking about the harvest and the 
angels doing the harvesting.  Jesus understood Christianity would be corrupted.  
When we look back, we can clearly see this.  This corruption would be revealed 
at the end of the age.   

Jesus definitely taught about the end of the age - his apostles had 
learned enough to specifically ask for signs:   
Matthew 24:3: (NIV) As Jesus was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples 
came to him privately. Tell us, they said, when will this happen, and what will be 
the sign of your coming and of the end of the age <165>?  
Even the disciples were interested in this subject.  Worshippers of God 
throughout the ages have been looking forward to an end to sin and death and 
accompanying suffering.  When will the end of this terrible age of suffering be?   
Jesus reminded his disciples that his care would be present for 
them and every Christian until the end of the age:  
Matthew 28:20: (NIV) and teaching them to obey everything I have commanded 
you. And surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age <165>. 
This beautiful verse shows the tenderness of Jesus.  He understood there would 
continue to be trouble throughout all of history.  We will distinguish that 
trouble from the specific trouble at the end of the age below.  He knew that 
those who followed him would be persecuted, even martyred.  He comforted 
all those who would follow him through the next 2,000 years. 
There are more Scriptures like this.  A search on the phrase last days gives us 
more, helping us to establish that the Bible teaches there is a time of the end.   
This leads to two more questions: 

What features indicate this time of the end so we can answer these questions? 
To answer this, we will focus on the prophecy in Daniel: 
Daniel 12:1-4: (KJV) 1And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which 
standeth for the children of thy people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was 
since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time thy people shall be delivered, 
every one that shall be found written in the book. 2And many of them that sleep in the dust of 
the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting 
contempt. 3And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that 
turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever. 4But thou, O Daniel, shut up the 
words, and seal the book, even to the time of the end: many shall run to and fro, and knowledge 
shall be increased. 
There is a lot of information here.  Let’s dissect these words and extract some 
of the characteristics of the end of the age: 
 
There shall be a time of trouble – what does this mean? 

 
Such as never was since there was a nation – it will be the worst in 
history.  The threat level will be the highest it has ever been. 

 
At that time thy people shall be delivered - it will precede the 
blessings of God’s kingdom – the end of the evil system will bring 

about the rejoicing of all of mankind. 

 
The prophecy will not be understood until the time of the end. 

 
Many shall run to and fro - a clue!  There are unprecedented 
opportunities to travel today.   

 
Knowledge shall be increased – exponentially!   

People often focus on the time of trouble.  This is not a happy scenario.   
We have an ominous ending of who knows what?   
So far, we have a very broad description of this time of trouble.   
Are we able to know specific details?  
Bible prophecy can be tricky because it is so interpretive.  We can look at 
specific verses from a specific perspective and come to specific conclusions, 
which will inevitably be…incorrect!   
The key to all of this is context.  So far, our foundation states: 
1.  The End Times are unique in ALL of history, and 
2.  This time would not be understood until it arrived.   
                              It would be a mystery until it was actually upon the world.

distinguished from trouble down through the 
ages by three things:  

This chapter in Amos talks about the features of the end days, like the

Amos 5:19: (KJV) 19As if a man did flee from a lion, and a bear met him; or went into the 
house, and leaned his hand on the wall, and a serpent bit him.  

These categories show the scope of trouble – it is worldwide and affects all 
aspects of everyone’s lives.   

Let’s look closer at a few of the categories  
of world trouble.   

Trouble will occur in a unique period of time: 
Matthew 24:20-22: (NASB) 20But pray that your flight will not be in the winter, or on a

1914 began World War I, which was clearly a significant time of trouble in 
 human history.  Never before had a world war occurred.    
(Source:

80 to 120 million:  The total number of

 These numbers are unprecedented in human history!

  62:  The number of sovereign nations in 1914.

The point of these statistics is that new countries come about by separating

The number of nations has more than tripled in the last 100 years. 
This scope of trouble has not happened in the history of humanity to the same

The rich will be exposed for their lack of love and concern: 
James 5:1-3: (NASB) 1Come now, you rich, weep and howl for your miseries which are coming 
upon you. 2Your riches have rotted and your garments have become moth-eaten. 3Your gold and 
your silver have rusted; and their rust will be a witness against you and will consume your flesh 
like fire. It is in the last days that you have stored up your treasure!  
Corporate influence in the world:  With power comes responsibility.  The rich 
through the ages have had a certain amount of power due to their wealth.   
This brings responsibility because wealth has political influence.  God 
remembers when this influence is used unkindly or selfishly.  God’s justice is 
based on careful recordkeeping.   
James 5:1-3 speaks of a time of reckoning for the rich - your gold and your 
silver have rusted and their rust will… consume your flesh like fire.  When the 
stock market crashed in 1929 in the United States, many committed suicide 
because they could not deal with the loss.  The despair of losing all was 
literally killing them.  
(Source:  https://www.globalissues.org/print/article/234) 
As of 2002(!), of the 100 largest economies in the world, 51 were corporations 
while only 49 were countries, based on a comparison of corporate sales and 
country gross domestic product (GDP).  (Editor’s note:  According to non-
governmental organization, Global Justice Now, as of 2018, 69 of the top 100 global 
  economic entities are corporations; the other 31 are countries.) 

In this era of globalization, marginalized people are becoming especially angry 
at the motives and operational methods of multinational corporations.   
Corporate-led globalization is being met with increasing protest and resistance.  
There is a rebellion against the power held by corporations.   
This power is not just economic, but also political.  They are influencing 
political movements and government officials, all without being subject to, or 
restrained by, election - not much different from dictatorship.  Corporations 
are even considered to have human rights!   
Has this ever happened in the history of humanity?  The point of this is to 
define a quality or feature that distinguishes the time of the end from all 
others.  Has there ever been an Amazon, Walmart or Microsoft or any other 
massive corporation?  No!  Back in the 1800s, we had the coal barons and the 
oil barons, the great banking empires, but that also was unprecedented and 
could be considered the beginning of these End Times.  Corporations have 
   evolved in our own time in ways we could not have imagined.   

Monetary problems:   
Ezekiel 7:19: (NASB) They will fling their silver into the streets

 Examples of trouble with silver and gold: 
 The Great Depression (1929-1941) – Starting in the United States as a 
leader in international trade, this affected the worldwide community.   
We continue to see in this the fact that since the end of the 19th 
century, the majority of the world is affected by such large events.   
This was the beginning of globalization, when economic trouble is no 
longer localized to one nation. 
 Inflation – We have seen waves of this even in our lifetime.  A dollar 
today will not buy the same amount as a dollar a year ago.  Inflation 
steals money from the people and shrinks the value of saved money in 
the bank.  This is trouble for the people of the world. 
 The Gold Standard versus fiat money (the value is not based on a gold or 
silver bar in the bank, but is a floating standard based on how much is 
printed by the government) – This depends on government decree and 
how our country measures up to others.  The value of our currency is 
determined by how much we can buy from others. 
Money can lose its value in two ways:  It can be stolen through inflation, 
but it is also worthless when there is nothing to buy.  We might have 
$100 in our hand, but if there is no bread, the $100 is not going to fill 
our stomachs; it becomes worthless. 

Has this ever happened in the history of humanity?  We are seeing these 
things all come together; is this coincidence?  No, it is a converging of all these 
elements as we move forward in God’s plan.  This near-global depression, 
waves of inflation, loss of a physical monetary standard, along with the 
continued waves of recession and boom are, once again, unprecedented in the 
amount of people affected.   

The widespread embracing of immoral behavior: 
2 Timothy 3:1-3: (NASB) 1But realize this, that in the last days difficult times will come. 
2For men will be lovers of self, lovers of money, boastful, arrogant, revilers, disobedient to

2 Timothy 3:4-7: (NASB) 4treacherous, reckless, conceited, lovers of pleasure rather than

This is the state of religion today.  It is interesting that the Apostle Paul brings

 Church attendance - is greatly reduced. 
 Ignorance of the Bible – especially here in the United States.  Even 50
