Three Unmistakable Signs You’re in a Toxic Work Environment, Bob Sutton INC. 
• 
If you're in a work environment, and you’re wondering whether it’s getting to 
you - here's the top three questions that you should ask yourself.  The first 
one is, is my well-being suffering?  Having trouble sleeping, feeling a little bit 
anxious, maybe having a family relationship problem?  To me that’s a sign 
you’ve got a long-term bullying problem.  The second one is kind of career 
performance effects.  There’s a lot of evidence that when people feel 
surrounded by jerks, or have a jerk who’s really getting to them that their 
performance suffers, they have trouble concentrating, they’re less creative, 
they don’t go the extra mile - that’s the second effect.  The third one - and 
this is one of those sort of contagion problems - there’s evidence that if 
you’re around a bunch of jerks - number one, you’re going to catch the disease 
and turn into a jerk, and number two, take it out on other people. 

1. Is my well-being suffering?   
2. Is my performance suffering?   
3. Am I catching the disease? 

We will describe Jesus’ work as his mission to bring people to the gospel and 
plant seeds of the kingdom.  He did not have a typical job, but he had work to 
do. 
During his typical “work day,” he showed us what our internal attitude 
should be: 
Matthew 22:34-40: (NASB) 34But when the Pharisees heard that Jesus had silenced the 
Sadducees, they gathered themselves together. 35One of them, a lawyer, asked him a question, 
testing him, 36Teacher, which is the great commandment in the Law? 
Jesus tirelessly defended God’s character and knew full well the next question 
was a setup.  What would I do if I knew I was being set up?   
Here is what Jesus did: 
37And he said to him, You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your 
soul, and with all your mind. 38This is the great and foremost commandment. 39The second is 
like it, You shall love your neighbor as yourself. 40On these two commandments depend the 
whole Law and the Prophets. 
He kept his emotions in check.  By telling them the highest truth, he stood his 
enemies in front of a self-reflection mirror. 
Stephen asks on our website:  I recently watched a YouTube video about 
purging occult objects from our home.  It made me feel concerned that studying 
natural and mathematical sciences is unsafe, but this extreme view suggests that 
any profession outside of divinity or ministry does not glorify God.   
Math and science are not unsafe.  The Bible is mathematical and proves 
science.  Most of us do not work for pay in the ministry.  We at Christian 
Questions, for example, are all volunteers.  Whenever possible, we want to 
choose a job that works along with our Christian integrity.  A casino or liquor 
store may not be the best place for a Christian to work.  Choose a job that has 
something decent about it and then work really hard at it. 
What if we just do not like our job?  Do we believe God provided it for us?  
Sometimes we learn Christlikeness through struggle more than when things are 
going well.  We have more reliance on God.  Not liking our job could be a good 
thing.  We have to rely on the Lord day-by-day and sometimes we do not 
have the perfect job. 
Do not be lazy: 
Proverbs 10:26: (NASB) Like vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes, so is the lazy one 
to those who send him.  
We have to work hard even if we are given something we do not like to do. 
Becca, a teacher, starts to tell her story:  My boss/principal was a bully, and 
unfortunately when you are in a position of power that goes unchecked, it's 
unbelievably hard to do anything about it.  My main strategy for dealing with 
him was avoidance unless I needed something from him.  For whatever reason, 
my department in the Arts was a specific target of cruelty, partially because 
there were many long-time teachers that felt that it was their duty to stand up 
to him.  That in and of itself caused me a lot of stress, because I felt that I 
should be as vocal and stand up for what was right; however I also knew that 

by doing that it would put me in the line of fire, and I really just wanted to 
 close my door and do my job… 
What if our job is an unfair environment?  Is God directing you to leave or 
are you just unhappy? 
1 Corinthians 7:21-24: (NASB) 21Were you called while a slave? Do not worry about it; but 
if you are able also to become free, rather do that. 22For he who was called in the Lord while a 
slave, is the Lord's freedman; likewise he who was called while free, is Christ's slave. 23You were 
bought with a price; do not become slaves of men. 24Brethren, each one is to remain with God 
in that condition in which he was called. 
The idea is even if we are a slave in the wordly environment, if we are called 
to Christ, we have a freedom other people do not have.  Bask in that freedom! 
Sometimes our freedom will be only in Christ, and sometimes we might be 
delivered from the circumstances.  Let us work on being happy either way. 

With our attitudes in the right place, what is the next step  
in being a light for Christ in the world of our work environment?   
It has been said that our lives are often self-fulfilling prophecies, and our work 
experiences are no exception.  The purpose for working is to be self-sufficient 
and that can come by squeaking by or by making a statement of excellence in 
our approach and our productivity! 
What is YOUR statement of excellence in your workplace or school? 
Excellence, Four Attributes of a Workplace Christian, Os Hillman 
• 
What really makes the difference in being a Christian in the workplace?  Well, 
I came up with four things.  The first thing is excellence.  God calls us to do 
our work with excellence.  In Daniel, chapter 2, (actually it is Daniel 1:20) it says 
that Daniel and his three friends Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego did their 
work ten times better than anyone else.  You see, if we don’t do our work 
with excellence we don’t earn the right to be able to have a voice in the 
marketplace.  If you do shoddy work people aren’t going to listen to you.  Let 
me encourage you that whatever you do, do it unto the Lord.   

Jesus’ Statement of Excellence: 
John 4:31-35: (NASB) 31Meanwhile the disciples were urging him, saying, Rabbi, eat. 32But 
he said to them, I have food to eat that you do not know about. 33So the disciples were saying 
to one another, No one brought him anything to eat, did he? 
Jesus’ focus was clearly higher than his followers as his mission never left his 
 mind.  If he missed a meal, he did not notice. 
34Jesus said to them, My food is to do the will of Him who sent me and to accomplish His work. 
35Do you not say, There are yet four months, and then comes the harvest? Behold, I say to you, 
lift up your eyes and look on the fields, that they are white for harvest. 
In other words, “My nourishment is to do God’s will.  We have God’s will to do 
everywhere.”  

To do the will of God is supposed to be our nourishment.  If I do 
not “live for my job” like Jesus did because my job is not in the 
ministry, per se, how does this “will of God” principle fit into 
my job and its requirements? 

Our goal should be keeping a high standard.  Honesty, integrity, punctuality, 
reliability.  Do all things as unto the Lord.  The workplace is no exception.  If 
God is our supervisor, we should be doing our best.  If we are doing His will, He 
is watching our actions, heart and mind.  My Christianity is being shown to Him 
by doing my work that has nothing to do with Him directly as if it has 
everything to do with Him directly.  If I am making widgets, I am working as if I 
 am making them for God. 
 We should emulate Joseph: 
• He worked diligently in Potiphar’s house 
under an adverse situation. 
• In prison, the jailer put him in charge of the 
other prisoners.  
• In service to Pharaoh he worked diligently 
and honored God in everything he did. 

Joseph showed us his Statement of Excellence.  It did not matter what his 
circumstance was; he would rise to the highest level he could because he 
   worked as unto God. 

How should Christians go about their work?  With a determined work ethic: 
1 Timothy 5:8: (NASB) But if anyone does not provide for his own, and especially for those 
of his household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.  
A work ethic has to be in place and engaged before you get there.  We, of all 
 people, should be the ones who step up and step out, even if it is difficult.   
We are to provide for our families.  There is a lot of generosity in Christianity 
and we want to help support one another, but it may not be the appropriate 
thing to do if someone is capable but chooses not to work.  The Apostle Paul 
warns against this and says that person is worse than an unbeliever.  
Becca continues:  Things got worse and worse as my boss would push ridiculous 
policies that didn't make sense.  He would lie, belittle and demean colleagues 
and students.  Many times it would be in front of only one or two people and he 
would just deny any wrongdoing.  I started to feel a little bit like I was going 
crazy when these terrible things are happening and there was NO recourse for 
the person who was behaving in this way and that would get me really riled up 
and angry.  I'd come home from school on a daily basis with a laundry list of 
 things that made me mad, and then I'd be reliving them all over again.   
It is hard to let a bad situation go; it is an exhausting cycle.  News flash!  We 
do not HAVE to live in that cycle; we can rise above it.  Striving for excellence 
 might help us. 
How else should Christians go about their work?  With a foundation of 
honesty: 
Proverbs 10:2: (NASB) Ill-gotten gains do not profit, but righteousness delivers from death.  
You can make a lot of money in illicit ways.  But it does not profit us from the 
standpoint of righteousness.  If in our workplace environment we are involved 
in anything shady, underhanded or something you would not tell your minister 
about, ask yourself what you are doing.  Everything less than above-board is 
 everything less than Christian.   
When I go to work, am I bringing my 
Christianity with me in such situations?  
Sometimes we can rationalize our way into 
bad behavior, making the ends justify the 
means.  We can be in a situation like, “I need 
to support my family, and therefore, I am 
going to do ‘this.’”  Is it something for which 
we could take Jesus with us?  If we could not 
 take him with us, we ought not to do it. 
Sometimes we can rationalize our way into bad behavior making the ends 
justify the means.  This is wrong: 
Proverbs 15:26-29: (NASB) 26Evil plans are an abomination to the LORD, but pleasant words 
are pure. 27He who profits illicitly troubles his own house, but he who hates bribes will live. 
28The heart of the righteous ponders how to answer, but the mouth of the wicked pours out evil 
things. 29The LORD is far from the wicked, but He hears the prayer of the righteous. 
Evil plans are an abomination to the LORD – this is serious!  

He who profits illicitly troubles his own house – this will bring trouble to our 
 family eventually, somehow. 
It is far easier to love righteousness than it is to hate iniquity, but that is our 
 standard through Jesus.   
We need to hate iniquity with the same energy as we love righteousness: 
Hebrews 1:9: (NASB) You have loved righteousness and hated lawlessness; therefore God, 
your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your companions. 
Theresa contributes:  Part of my job is to plan our company's 
annual conference.  Historically, we've held this event in the 
same city as our corporate offices; however, for our 60th 
anniversary, our President wanted to do something bigger 
and better to celebrate.  She proposed Las Vegas and she 
ended up opening the conference with a welcome toast and 
ended it with how we were going to have fun to celebrate and 
"what happens in Vegas, stays in  Vegas," basically condoning any 
 behavior that may happen.   
There are certain lies in life that come about.  One of the great lies in all of 
history was Satan’s lie to Adam, You will not surely die.  This was a lie, and we 
see the trouble it caused.  This slogan is the same kind of lie - a rationalization 
that is as untrue as can be.  We all know that if we have committed an 
indiscretion, it does not just stay where we committed it.  It follows us home 
 and eats us up until we do something to repent and fix it. 
I worked in a factory years ago.  I am a hard worker and was diligent, and a 
supervisor said, “I have never seen anyone with your productivity.”  But the 
people around me said, “You are making us look bad.  Stop, slow down.”  How 
do we handle peer pressure when we are trying to keep our work ethic 
 honoring the Lord? 
Rick’s dad’s answer in that same scenario was, “I get paid to work eight hours, 
and I owe that to my employer.  No reflection on you; I just need to go to 
work.”  If it is appropriate to explain about God at this point, do so!  We do not 
compromise because other people feel bad.  We do not DO it to make them 
 feel or look bad, we do it to bring honor to God and in a humble way. 
How should Christians go about their work?  With a godly focus: 
Ephesians 6:5-8: (NASB) 5Slaves, be obedient to those who are your masters according to 
the flesh, with fear and trembling, in the sincerity of your heart, as to Christ; 6not by way of 
eye service, as men-pleasers, but as slaves of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart. 7with 
good will render service, as to the Lord, and not to men, 8knowing that whatever good thing 
each one does, this he will receive back from the Lord, whether slave or free. 
Be obedient with respect and sincerity - With good will render service, as to 
    the Lord, and not to men. 

How should Christians go about their work?  With a mastery seeking 
approach: 
Proverbs 22:29: (NASB) Do you see a man skilled in his work? He will stand before kings; he 
will not stand before obscure men.  
Usually those who work hard stand out.  I started out on the production line of 
a furniture company, put my head down and worked hard.  I ended up as the 
General Manager of the shop several years later.  How did that happen?  I 
worked hard and did what I was supposed to do. 

We have to work hard because we represent Christ,  
but do we always have to be happy about it?   
While it is not a requirement to be happy about our everyday work 
environment, we are to be contented in the fact that God has provided a way 
for us to support ourselves.  We just established the importance of pursuing 
excellence, so now let us look around the edges at some of the non-production 
parts of work that really matter.   
 Integrity, Four Attributes of a Workplace Christian, Os Hillman 
• 
The second thing is ethics and integrity.  God called us to do our work with 
ethics and integrity.  Integrity is what you do behind closed doors.  Is it the 
same thing in public as what you do behind closed doors?  Psalm 51, David 
writes that “God desires truth in the inward parts.”  That means whatever I 
do out there is the same behind the closed doors.  You want to be a person of 
integrity.   

This is sometimes easier said than done.  It is a 
battle between the ears!  Keep battling and asking 
for forgiveness, continually working at being better. 

There are voices that seek to influence everywhere around us and 
all of them are not good.  We need to select the right things to 
listen to. 
Here is Jesus’ example of selective hearing: 
John 8:25-26: (NASB) 25So they were saying to him, Who are you? Jesus said 
to them, What have I been saying to you from the beginning? 26I have many things 
to speak and to judge concerning you, but He who sent me is true; and the things 
which I heard from Him, these I speak to the world. 
The things which I heard from Him, these I speak to the world – “The things I 
hear from God are what you hear from me.”   
Jesus painted an abundantly clear picture – carefully select that which will 
influence you. 
Becca continues:  I really felt that the negativity and toxicity slowly started to 
affect me as a person.  The other end of things is it led to LOTS of gossip, but 
the worst part is that it didn't feel like you were gossiping.  You were sharing 
information with a colleague to warn them, or keep them updated on the most

Sunday nights before school started I would feel sick to my stomach and the

I can relate to that.  At one time I worked in an environment where

 was deeply disturbing. 
Tricia adds:  As we go through the Scriptures about what we should be like,

Jesus in these next verses shows that he did NOT do all of the things he was 
capable of: 
Luke 12:13-15: (NASB) 13Someone in the crowd said to him, Teacher, tell my brother to 
divide the family inheritance with me. 14But he said to him, Man, who appointed me a judge or 
arbitrator over you? 15Then he said to them, Beware, and be on your guard against every form 
of greed; for not even when one has an abundance does his life consist of his possessions. 
Jesus could have read the hearts of these men and given them equity, but that 
was not his job.  He was not trying to fix the world, but rather to bring 
individuals out of the world to a higher level. 
How do we determine what voices to follow at work, especially if our 
employer may be sending compromising signals? 
We have to always be on guard against shortcuts, lying and compromising, 
but if the boss tells us to do whatever goes against our Christian 
conscience, we need to remind him or her we cannot do that because it would 
not be right. 
We can and should speak up, even though it might cost us our job.  God wants 
to test our loyalty to His righteous standards.  We are to be loyal to Him before 
the job, during the job and after the job. 
Selective hearing means listening to the things that will guide us into the right 
way, not the compromised or dishonest way. 
If they could work as unto God being “slaves,” we certainly can do it having 
a choice of what to do: 
Colossians 3:22-25: (NASB) 22Slaves, in all things obey those who are your masters on earth, 
not with external service, as those who merely please men, but with sincerity of heart, fearing 
the Lord. 23Whatever you do, do your work heartily, as for the Lord rather than for men, 
24knowing that from the Lord you will receive the reward of the inheritance. It is the Lord Christ 
whom you serve. 25For he who does wrong will receive the consequences of the wrong which he 
has done, and that without partiality.   
The Apostle talked to the Colossians, Ephesians and Corinthians about slavery – 
this is common – he was telling everyone we must do our job with sincerity of 
heart because God is our ultimate boss.  The Apostle said this to all groups of 
Christians; He said that to all of us.  This is the selective hearing we have to 
have. 
This advice encourages full dedication with the assurance that any evil will 
receive its reward…maybe not in this life, but God does not allow evil to go 
unchallenged.  The Christian slave was to listen as unto God.   
Theresa continues:  When our President proposed Las Vegas, she asked for a 
vote on keeping the event local or moving it to Vegas.  It was quite difficult to 
NOT vote in favor of the location.  She went around the conference room table 
and asked each Leadership Team member to verbally vote “yes” or “no” and

  difficulties in planning.   

How should a Christian worker listen?  With ears tuned to a Holy Spirit-
driven spiritual conscience:  
Romans 8:13-15: (NASB) 13For if you are living according to the flesh, you must die; but if 
by the Spirit you are putting to death the deeds of the body, you will live. 14For all who are 
being led by the Spirit of God, these are sons of God. 15For you have not received a spirit of 
slavery leading to fear again, but you have received a spirit of adoption as sons by which we cry 
out, Abba! Father! 
Gossip in the workplace can be damaging, and we need to avoid it.  Please see 
September 19, 2016, CQ Episode #936, “Does Gossip Really Hurt Anyone?”  It 
 can lead to putting down others to try to get ahead in the workplace.   
 God’s Spirit provides direction.  Listen to those in power at work heartily.   
BUT if there is a need to reconsider actions based in Christian integrity, 
allow God’s Spirit to show you, not your emotions: 
Isaiah 30:20-21: (NASB) 20Although the Lord has given you bread of privation and water of 
oppression, He, your Teacher will no longer hide Himself, but your eyes will behold your 
Teacher. 21Your ears will hear a word behind you, This is the way, walk in it, whenever you turn 
to the right or to the left. 

Our productivity and our hearing must be Christlike  
as we pursue excellence.  Does that cover everything?    
As usual there is always something else to add to the picture.  Thus far, we 
have spoken about being an example through determination, action and 
responsiveness.  What about the power of our words in the workplace? 
Service, Four Attributes of a Workplace Christian, Os Hillman 
• 
The third area is service.  The Bible says that if you want to be great among 
them, then you must be servant of all.  That’s what Jesus did.  After all, it 
was the servants that saw that first miracle that Jesus did with the wine.  So 
you and I must be servants and serving people in the marketplace, solving 
problems.   

Jesus spoke of the things of God and sometimes those things were difficult.   
His words ALWAYS served a purpose: 
John 6:52-53: (NASB) 52Then the Jews began to argue with one another, saying, How can 
this man give us his flesh to eat? 53So Jesus said to them, Truly, truly, I say to you, unless you 
eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you have no life in yourselves. 
Jesus was not afraid to say those things that would be hard to hear.  Some 
things hurt his reputation and he lost followers.   
Becca continues:  Leaving that job has been life-changing in a lot of ways, and I 
know that people who have really awful, hostile work environments and bosses 
who are bullies don't always have the option to quit.  I am blessed enough to be 
married and have someone else to support me if I wasn't able to find work right 
away.  But for some of the other friends I have that are in these really terrible 
work situations I encourage them to just get out.  I don't want the environment 
and the people at my job to determine the kind of person that I am, and 
because I wasn't strong enough to withstand all of the terrible things around 
me, it was really in my best interest to just get out. 
In my bad work environment years ago, it got inside my head and I could not 
manage it.  I was the primary breadwinner in my home with small children, and 
when when another job opportunity dropped in my lap I ran to it, seeing God 
giving me a way out.  It was overtaking my mind and it was too much.  I was so 
 glad for the opportunity to get away, but it does not always work out that way. 
Jesus also spoke things of God that were encouraging.  His words always 
served a purpose: 
John 15:7-11: (NASB) 7If you abide in me, and my words abide in you, ask whatever you wish,

We should speak encouraging, strong words with the sense of bringing the 
environment up higher.  Be recognized as one who has something different in 
 our lives. 
He spoke of things of God that were even harsh when necessary.  His words 
always served a purpose: 
Matthew 23:27: (NASB) Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like

No minced words, “You are hypocrites!”  He was harsh but they needed to hear 
this. 
Theresa ends:  One of our vendors, a married man, brought

The “What happens in Vegas stays in Vegas” mentality is dangerous to our

Jesus said things that were hard to hear, he said things that were encouraging 
and things that were harsh.  But we cannot read the heart like Jesus, so how do 
 we know when to speak difficult or encouraging things of God?   
I had an experience working in a woodworking shop years ago with a lot of guys 
who did not care about their words at all – they were very crude.  One day the 
most senior worker in the shop once again said harsh words against my 
Heavenly Father.  I went up to him and told him these words hurt me, and did 
he realize he was putting down God?  I wasn’t sure how he was going to react.  
Guess what?  He apologized!  He really didn’t mean it; it had become rote – 
words he didn’t even know he was saying.  After that, he was much more 
 careful and showed respect to me and I showed respect to him. 
About a year after I left my bad job, I was laid off at the new job.  The day 
after I got laid off, my old boss called me back to work!  In that year, the Lord 
allowed me to do a lot of growing up.  I was different and had the attitude of, 
“Not this time!”  I worked hard, I was eventually promoted to General Manager 
and the whole environment got better – not perfect, but better.  Even the 
prevalent office lying started to go down because God allowed me to grow up 
 in between.  Stand up for things and things can happen!  
 Here is a recap of what we have discussed, all found in these next verses… 
Our workplace attitude - another slave reference, this time addressed to 
the masters: 
Colossians 4:1-6: (NASB) 1Masters, grant to your slaves justice and fairness, knowing that

3praying at the same time for us as well, that God will open up to us a door for the word, so

4that I may make it clear in the way I ought to speak. 5Conduct yourselves with wisdom toward

We may even have the opportunity to witness in the workplace, if anything just

Proverbs 14:23: (NASB) In all labor there is profit, but mere talk leads only to poverty.  

Attitude, excellence, attentiveness and our words.   
What else could we possibly need to focus on? 
Our final look will be into the culmination of all of those things as we now 
examine the character that we bring to work each day.  Jesus obviously was 
always pure in his approach, and we must strive to take what he did and said

Becca ends:  We are called to be different and to stand out and as

      Signs and wonders, Four Attributes of a Workplace Christian, Os Hillman 
• 
Fourth, signs and wonders.  Acts Chapter 5 tells us that the apostles did 
miraculous signs and wonders in the public colonnade where the people could 
see them.  Jesus never invited someone into the synagogue to get healed or to 
get prayed for or to solve a problem.  He was in the marketplace every day.  
He was out with the people, and so that’s a great lesson for us.  If you’re a 
person who wants to be a marvel in the marketplace, you want to be a person 
of excellence, you want to be a person of integrity, you want to be a person 
that serves others, and finally, you want to be a person that does signs and 
wonders.  Maybe God will give you an idea for a new invention or a better way 
of doing something in your workplace, or just praying for someone.  There are 
a lot of ways that you can do that one.   
Are we supposed to do miracles in our workplace?  No, we are in the age of 
example, not of performing miracles.  We are to live a lifestyle that is 
dramatically different from those around us.  What is the sign of your 
Christianity?  What about you gives others pause to wonder about what makes 
you so different? 

Here are some of Jesus’ actions: 
Matthew 12:1-7: (NASB) 1At that time Jesus went through the grainfields on the Sabbath, 
and his disciples became hungry and began to pick the heads of grain and eat. 2But when the 
Pharisees saw this, they said to him, Look, your disciples do what is not lawful to do on a 
Sabbath. 
The Pharisees were like people at work who are always criticizing our 
efforts towards excellence: 
3But he said to them, Have you not read what David did when he became hungry, he and his 
companions, 4how he entered the house of God, and they ate the consecrated bread, which was 
not lawful for him to eat nor for those with him, but for the priests alone? 5Or have you not 
read in the Law, that on the Sabbath the priests in the temple break the Sabbath and are 
innocent? 6But I say to you that something greater than the temple is here. 7But if you had 
known what this means, I desire compassion, and not a sacrifice, you would not have condemned 
the innocent. 
“David did the same thing.  How come you are not complaining about David?  
There is something bigger here than the Law (pointing to himself).”   
But if you had known what this means, (these next words are from God in the 
Old Testament) I desire compassion, and not a sacrifice, you would not have 
condemned the innocent – in other words, “You are missing the point of the 

thing you are complaining about.”  Jesus showed them they needed to rise 
above where they were. 
The excellence Jesus taught his followers to have was based on a higher 
standard.  In our workplace environment, always be the “you” that is following 
Jesus, not some other “you.”  Jesus himself was his disciples’ teacher.  We 
should deeply care, and not just show up.   
I went to a five-month course on how to go into business for yourself.  There 
were 16 adults there learning this process.  It was an open environment and we 
were trying to help each other become successful.  One day, one of the 
students came up to me and asked if we could get together to talk.  He invited 
me to his house.  He said, “I could see your faith in the class, and I am very 
troubled in my life.  I know there is one other woman in class who talks about 
Christianity all the time; I already met with her.  But there is something 
different about you.  I’m contemplating suicide.  Can you talk to me?”  I didn’t 
even say any words in the class to witness, but I was there.  I shared the good 
news about the gospel, about the call to follow in Jesus’ footsteps.  He 
instantly was attracted, changed his life and started being the man he could be 
in following Christ.  I was so thankful he asked if I could help. 
Preach the gospel.  Use words if necessary. – Rick’s Uncle Steve 
 We have to bring a Christlike character to work. 
Have a character that exudes diligence: 
Proverbs 13:4: (NASB) The soul of the sluggard craves and gets nothing, but the soul of the 
diligent is made fat.  
The sluggard wants, wants and wants, but sometimes you just have to pick up 
the shovel and start digging.  Go to work!  Exude diligence!  Be the first one,

 better environment, so let’s be diligent. 
Have a character that breathes godly contentment in all experiences:  
1 Timothy 6:6-7: (NASB) 6But godliness actually is a means of great gain when accompanied

of it either. 
Godliness and contentment have to be combined.  We can be godly by showing 
attention to God and wanting His will, but we can be restless.  Once we are 
content, knowing that God takes care of us even when it is uncomfortable, that 
 is what brings great gain. 
Be serious in your workplace – go beyond what is required – plow through 
challenges – finish: 
2 Timothy 4:5-8: (NASB) 5But you, be sober in all things, endure hardship, do the work of 
an evangelist, fulfill your ministry. 6For I am already being poured out as a drink offering, and

John 17:1-4: (NASB) 1Jesus spoke these things; and lifting up his eyes to heaven, he said,

How Do You Manage Failure? (Part II)
Luke 22:32: (NASB) But I have prayed for you, that your faith may not fail;
and you, when once you have turned again, strengthen your brothers.
Failure, as everyone knows, is an unlooked for and unwelcome
commodity in life. It disrupts our plans, impedes our progress, upsets
our feelings and is generally intrusive to our lives. As a result of failure’s
glowing resume, we often do whatever we can to avoid it, and when we
experience it we often try to soft peddle its impact or even hide its
presence. All in all, these descriptions of and reactions to failure are
really quite unfortunate. Failure gets too bad a rap. It is judged too
harshly.
A few weeks ago, we began a journey towards a better
understanding of failure.
In that journey, we began to see the place
failure holds in our lives and the value it can bring us. Let’s get back to
it, for success begins when we understand our failures!
The beginning, Life After Failure, Evan Hansen, TEDx Talk
•
Let me tell you a story. Twenty-two years ago, a baby boy named
Gabriel was born, and due to an incredibly early birth his precious life
was snatched away almost immediately after it was given to him. The
next year the mother was pregnant once again, and because of her
first failed pregnancy the doctors knew that safeguards needed to be
put in place. Among these precautions, the doctors had the mother
spend 108 days lying in a hospital bed in order for the new baby to be
born. Now in the end, their efforts turned out to be successful, and
even though the baby was still born early, he lived. Now I am telling
you this because I am that baby boy. I should not be standing up here
today, but I am because of my parent’s determination to raise a child,
and because of the doctor’s abilities to overcome the same medical
failures that led to my brother’s death.
Build the road through failure with your failures! Failure is good if you choose
for it to be. For most of us it is debilitating, humiliating, frustrating,
embarrassing, but we learn the big things through failure.

Sometimes we fail because we just do not know. The simple solution is to
learn so we can be better or do better.
Last time we discussed failure in relation to God’s plan. God has a Day of
Judgment planned, and in that “day” (a time period, not 24 hours) there will
be success and failure. The Scriptures tell us the kind of failure for which God
will require accountability and those He will not.
To get God’s perspective on how He views failure from a lack of knowledge, in
Part I we started reviewing the Parable of the Sower. Jesus talked about four
kinds of seed being sown. We related each type of seed to a different type of
failure.
Here is failure due to a lack of knowledge:
Mark 4:15: (NASB) These are the ones who are beside the road where the word is sown; and
when they hear, immediately Satan comes and takes away the word which has been sown in
them.
There was no opportunity for the seed to start to take root, as it never got into
the ground and Satan snatched it away. God’s word is not even allowed to
take root in the hearts of many. The entrance of sin caused God’s blessings to
NOT be fully extended to all. God allowed this!
Does God judge the world based on a lack of knowledge? A lot of Christianity
preaches this, saying billions of humanity will burn in hell because they did not
know any better. (This is not what the Scriptures teach.)
Look at this prophecy of God’s future kingdom, as it explains the role of
knowledge:
Isaiah 11:9: (NASB) They will not hurt or destroy in all My holy mountain, for the earth
will be full of the knowledge of the LORD as the waters cover the sea.
In the future, knowledge will be abundant and everywhere.
Yes, you have some responsibility for a lack of knowledge, but it will not be
hard to fix as long as you are humble enough to say, “I did not know; I better
learn!”

If you are immature, recognize you have growing up to do and be willing to
grow up. Build that road through failure with your failures!
I had an amazing experience and Rick’s parents were there to help me
out. Here I was a new Christian, reading the Scriptures and striving to
honor God in my life, and I was privileged to be able to live with Rick’s
parents for about six months. What I saw were examples of maturity,
what it takes to honor God, how you live a life. I had to have the hands-
on “watch and see” so I could draw that lesson and implement it.
That was an “It is time for Jonathan to grow up” lesson! We all have those
experiences that help us grow up. We often fail because we are not mature
enough. But once that failure is in place, we are to make it a positive. “I do
not want to be immature with that anymore; time to change my actions,
reactions or approach.”
Failure due to immaturity can be overcome and is not the worst kind of failure.
Look around you at those who are more mature. Like children, imitate the
spiritual maturity around you.
What about God’s Day of Judgment? Will He come down harshly on failure due
to immaturity?
Mark 4:16-17: (NASB) 16In a similar way these are the ones on whom seed was sown on the
rocky places, who, when they hear the word, immediately receive it with joy; 17and they have
no firm root in themselves, but are only temporary; then, when affliction or persecution arises
because of the word, immediately they fall away.
The first seed was taken by Satan. Now this seed could take root but is choked
out by the individual themself due to a desire for comfort in the face of
adversity. It has the ability for growth but does not have the strength to
overcome what is around it.

How does God react to immaturity in the future? Let’s look at another
prophecy:
Zechariah 8:23: (NASB) Thus says the LORD of hosts, in those days ten men from all the
nations will grasp the garment of a Jew, saying, let us go with you, for we have heard that
God is with you.
This is a tremendous display of maturity - “The way I have done it does not get
me where I need to go. Obviously, God is with you and I want to be with God,
so therefore I want to be with you.”
How humbling it will be for the nations to respect Israel because of the special
relationship they have with our Heavenly Father.
God will give the world the opportunity to grow up.
There are two more types of failure we will review:

Next up is failure due to weakness –
is this kind of failure worse than lack of knowledge and immaturity?
Failure due to weakness does delve into another pathway that we have not
talked about yet, and this pathway can be a real eye-opener. Failures due to
lack of knowledge and immaturity are dealt with by acquiring knowledge and
by growing up – failure due to weakness requires a lot more personal
responsibility.
This type of failure can come upon us even when we are mature and
experienced and can be a serious eye-opener to help us with exponential
growth. (This can really humble you! You may not be as strong as you
thought!)
Let’s review an example of a massive failure –
the Apostle Peter denying Jesus:
Matthew 26:33-35: (NASB) 33But Peter said to him, even though all
may fall away because of you, I will never fall away. 34Jesus said to him,
Truly I say to you that this very night, before a rooster crows, you will
deny me three times. 35Peter said to him, even if I have to die with you,
I will not deny you. All the disciples said the same thing too.
Peter plainly said he would stay by Jesus’ side, no matter
what. “I am strong enough to handle it. Not me – I won’t
fall away.” We believe his heart was right, his focus was
clear and he was serious.
Our failures due to weakness are often set up in a way that we really do know
the right answer before we end up giving and living the wrong answer.
Peter’s response was emphatic that he would not deny Jesus even if he had to
die with him.
You would think after being with Jesus for years, Peter would know whatever
Jesus said came to pass. He should have taken a second look at Jesus’ words,
but his emotions got the best of him.
Later that same night:
Matthew 26:69-74: (NASB) 69…and a servant-girl came to him and said, you too were with
Jesus the Galilean. 70But he denied it before them all, saying, I do not know what you are talking
about.
I do not know what you are talking about - He starts with a general denial.
This is a convenient way to try to avoid an issue and move on.
71When he had gone out to the gateway, another servant-girl saw him and said to those who
were there, this man was with Jesus of Nazareth. 72And again he denied it with an oath, I do
not know the man.

The denial escalates. He wanted to move away from the people so he would not
have to deal with this, but they caught him anyway.
He denied it with an oath, I do not know the man – He adds solemnity to the denial and
is specific. When we get into these situations, we are like Peter and tend to
pile onto our failure instead of admitting it and backing away.
73A little later the bystanders came up and said to Peter, surely you too are one of them; for
even the way you talk gives you away. 74Then he began to curse and swear, I do not know the
man!
Now he is angry, emphatic and lashing out at those around
him. He adds cursing to an over-the-top emotional reaction
since just denying was not enough. He entered into a massive
failure.
And immediately a rooster crowed. Luke 22:61: (NASB) The Lord turned
and looked at Peter. Matthew 26:75: (NASB) 75And Peter remembered
the word which Jesus had said, before a rooster crows, you will deny me
three times. And he went out and wept bitterly.
Peter had no place to go. He tried to deny. He tried to be
specific in his denial with an oath. Then he got over-the-top
and out of character, but when Jesus looked at him, he knew. You can see his
character. He had a huge failure, but when confronted he went out and wept
bitterly.
Peter’s circumstances overwhelmed his strength and he fell
prey to what was around him – the pressure of the
moment. He just was not strong enough.
I fell to fear and peer pressure. In high school, two young guys asked if I party.
They had beer and I liked beer when I was in high school, so sure! I went to
their car and they pulled out a joint, which I was not expecting. In my mind, I
was NEVER going to go down THAT road and do drugs because I thought that
was stupid. I pretended to smoke and they told me I was not doing it right.
The peer pressure made me fall into the weakness of the moment. The
problem with that moment is that it lasted eight years. From that moment of
weakness and failure, I went downhill fast. It was so sad.
This is a typical story of the human experience, where we do something or
have something happen in our lives and get stuck in it. The strength of the pull
of the vortex is too strong to pull out of. Sometimes the remedy for our failure
due to weakness comes much later.
The powerful intervening words and challenge of Jesus:
John 21:17: (NASB) 17He said to him the third time, Simon, son of
John, do you love me? Peter was grieved because he said to him the
third time, do you love me? And he said to him, Lord, you know all
things; you know that I love you. Jesus said to him, tend my sheep.
The response of Jesus to Peter’s failure was to look at him to show that Jesus
trusted in him, even though he blundered so completely on that night when

Jesus was abandoned by everyone. Jesus knew Peter’s heart. That is the
beauty of the remedy. “I know your heart. I know that is not what you meant
to do. I know you are weak. Do you love me?” He asked three times, the
same number of times Peter denied Jesus. (Incidentally, Jesus originally called
Peter to follow him three times.)
Only those who dare to fail greatly can ever achieve greatly. ― Robert F.
Kennedy
Peter was a great example of this. He grew up to be a powerful example of
Christlikeness.
The beauty of failure, Life After Failure, Evan Hansen, TEDx Talk
•
Now as I grew up with the knowledge that my very existence stemmed from
adversity, I began to believe that I should do everything in my power to avoid
failure, but somewhere along the line I began to see the beauty of failure.
I began to realize that we are not defined by how we succeed, but that we are
defined by how we fail. Now at some point in time, every one of us has
failed; there’s no denying it. And while logic might dictate that failure is
something to avoid, it is imperative to understand that personal failure is one
of the most important building blocks necessary to create positive changes in
this world. It’s also important to understand that failure is not the same as
quitting or using excuses to validate falling short of our potential. Embracing
failure involves understanding that each time we do not succeed we can use
our failures as leverage to strengthen our resolve and to face our obstacles
with new found knowledge and fresh perspectives.
A failure due to weakness remedy:
2 Corinthians 4:7-12: (NASB) 7But we have this treasure in earthen vessels, so that the
surpassing greatness of the power will be of God and not from ourselves; (Humility comes first…)
8we are afflicted in every way, but not crushed; perplexed, but not despairing; 9persecuted, but
not forsaken; struck down, but not destroyed; 10always carrying about in the body the dying of
Jesus, so that the life of Jesus also may be manifested in our body. (Changing the source of our
strength is second.)
We might think that once we recognize our failures due to weakness, we can
change them. Sometimes our weaknesses will never go away, so we have to
learn to compensate for them. If you know you are weak in a particular area,
here is a simple solution – do not go there anymore! Avoid it!

Will God’s plan treat failure because of weakness
with eternal harshness in His future judgment?
Failure due to weakness is a hallmark of the human race, and it makes sense to
many Christians that God would focus on and attack such a hallmark. However,
when we look at the Scriptures on this type of failure related to God’s
judgment, we see an entirely different story.
The one thing, Best Motivational Video 2015, Power of Choice, Tony Robbins
•
What is the single force that controls the quality of your life? If there was one
gift that our Creator has given us or the universe, whatever you believe, what
is the one power that you have right now in this moment that can change
everything? You have it, I have it, we all have it. This one singular individual
power that can change anything in our life regardless of what’s happened to
us. And I know you know the answer - the answer is the power of choice. The
one thing we have in this world is we can’t control the events, but we can
choose what to focus on, we can choose what things mean and we can choose
what to do. Those three choices, those three decisions, really control our life.
It’s not so much the conditions of our life that control our destiny as much as
the decisions of our life.
The way to begin to cope with failure due to weakness is to make the choice to
cope with it and rise above – do something different. If it is an area of
continual weakness, just do not go there anymore. Set up roadblocks.
On April 24, 2017, we made a podcast called “Virtual Sex and Pornography –
Does God Care,” and for many people, this is a problem that cannot be
controlled. It gets hold of you and ruins you. The answer is: SHUT THE DOOR.
You are too weak to be able to cope with it. Close the door and walk the other
way. This is a choice.

With the level of the world’s human weaknesses so overwhelming, it may seem
like God messed up.
Back to the explanation for the Parable of the Sower –
the third group:
Mark 4:18-19: (NASB) 18And others are the ones on whom seed was
sown among the thorns; these are the ones who have heard the word,
19but the worries of the world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the desires for other things
enter in and choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
First we had seeds stolen away by Satan, and then seeds that were choked out.
Now we have seeds that grow among thorns. This gives people a place where
they can find biblical answers to the dilemmas of their lives taking root but are
just too weak to flourish – there is too much in the way! Failure due to
weakness. This is what happens to so many people who hear the gospel. It
sounds good, but they just do not have the strength to hold on and find the
depth of the message.
The worries of the world, and the deceitfulness of riches - Those who are part
of the “Prosperity Gospel” should read this carefully! If we earnestly pray to
God, He will give us everything He wants for us, not everything we want.
Failure should be our teacher, not our undertaker. Failure is delay, not defeat.
It is a temporary detour, not a dead end. Failure is something we can avoid only
by saying nothing, doing nothing, and being nothing. ― Denis Waitley
Success and failure, Success, Failure and the Drive to Keep Creating, Elizabeth
Gilbert, TED Talk
•
So, think of it like this…for most of your life you live out your existence here
in the middle of the chain of human experience where everything is normal
and reassuring and regular, but failure catapults you abruptly way out over
here into the blinding darkness of disappointment. Success catapults you just
as abruptly but just as far, way out over here into the equally-blinding glare
of fame and recognition and praise. One of the fates is objectively seen by
the world as bad and the other one is objectively seen by the world as good,
but your subconscious is completely incapable of discerning the difference
between bad and good. The only thing that it is capable of feeling is the
absolute value of this emotional equation - the exact distance that you have
been flung from yourself, and there’s a real equal danger in both cases of
getting lost out there in the hinterlands of the psyche.
We can easily fail when we get outside of our comfort zone.
First, God’s remedy was prepared ahead of time:
1 Peter 2:9-12: (NASB) 9But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood,
a holy nation, a people for God’s own possession, so that you may proclaim
the excellencies of Him who has called you out of darkness into His
marvelous light; 10for you once were not a people, but now you are the
people of God; you had not received mercy, but now you have received
mercy.
This gives an active description of what true Christians are called to do and to
be. You are catapulted out of your normal realm of being and sometimes that

is uncomfortable. You have received a very powerful mercy. God’s remedy for
the world is going to come through true Christianity.
Second, Christians are called out of the world and up from the world to be
presently trained for a future work of ministering, encouraging and leading
a weak and sinful world of men to God:
11Beloved, I urge you as aliens and strangers to abstain from fleshly lusts which wage war against
the soul.
Fight against your weaknesses! This is a present-day challenge for every
Christian. Our managing of our own failures now will help us guide the world
later. We are learning how to be powerful guides for the sake of God through
Christ. We have a world of miserable failures that need to be led to God after
their resurrection. You, as a true Christian, will be helping in that mission!
12Keep your behavior excellent among the Gentiles, so that in the thing in which they slander
you as evildoers, they may because of your good deeds, as they observe them, glorify God in
the day of visitation.
The people who are talking bad about you are the same people who will be
glorifying God because of your example in the day of visitation, the Day of
Judgment. This is in the kingdom Jesus taught us to pray for (Thy kingdom
come, Thy will be done on earth…). We are told in 2 Peter 3:8 (quoting from
Psalms 90:4) that a day with the Lord is like a thousand years. In this day
(time period) of visitation, God through Christ and the church (the faithful
followers of Jesus) will help all humanity to understand what they need to do
to have everlasting life.
The present experiences of a Christian are in contradiction to the world around
them, which causes grief and persecution. If you are not contrary to the world
around you, we would suggest you look in the mirror and ask, “How did I
represent Christ today?” Not, “How did I represent the things I like about
Christ so my friends wouldn’t be offended today?” Our lives should be out of
character with the world around us.
This text tells us that those in the world will at that future time be able to
recognize and respond to the experiences of the future priesthood. This means
the failures of weakness and blindness of this age will be wiped away from
their lives. They will be able to overcome the weakness.

When it comes to God’s judgment upon the world, failure due to weakness will
not preclude having an opportunity for life. How do they glorify God in the day
of visitation? Because they are able to grow up into Christ and become more
righteous and upstanding in their focus. God will not judge humanity based on
weakness.
For us as Christians, we need to fight those weaknesses so we can be of help in
the future. Go to the word of God and lean on His power so we can be lifted
up. We want to learn to grow from failure due to weakness.
There is one last pathway that failure gets us on –
the pathway of choice – why did we save this one for last?
Failure due to our personal choices is the most insidious kind of failure as it
implies that there was ample knowledge of the situation, sufficient maturity to
recognize the gravity of the situation and no inherent weakness that
overwhelmed us in facing the situation. This level of failure (failure due to
personal choices) acts against righteousness and godliness simply because it
wants to. Deception can bring us failure on any of the first three paths, but
NOT ON THIS ONE! Here failure is a choice!
“If Loving You Is Wrong,” (Partial verse) Luther Ingram

That is an example of the idolatry of self-will. “The sacred covenant of

Sins of choice always have the most clear-cut final consequences if there is no

The Apostle Paul back when he was known as Saul of Tarsus:

Decisions equal destiny, Best Motivational Video 2015, Power of Choice, Tony
Robbins
•
So, decisions equal destiny. It’s not our conditions, it’s our decisions. So, if
we want a new life, if we want a new experience, we’ve got to make new
choices. If you don’t like the way your career is or your business is, change it.
If you don’t like your body, change it. If you don’t like your relationship,
change you first, because if you change it you’ll bring “you” to the next one.
Maybe it’s time to change it, too, but change yourself first. If you want to
change any of your life you have the choice, so there is no right or wrong. I
just want to make you aware in this breakthrough session that everything in
our life changes the moment we make a decision. I mean a real decision. A

This was a wakeup call for Saul, and I had a wakeup call after eight years. It

dramatic; it can be a slow and steady process. Jonathan did not wake up one

difficulties.
No, I went through all the stages of failure.
That is the beauty of it. He went through the stages of failure. In other
words, each stage was another stepping stone to finding real meaning in life.
That is what failure is supposed to do for us as Christians. That is what we
have to focus on.

Build your home, Success, Failure and the Drive to Keep Creating,
Elizabeth Gilbert, TED
•
Look, I don’t know where you rightfully live, but I know that there is
something in this world that you love more than you love yourself. Something
worthy, by the way, so addiction and infatuation don’t count because we all
know that those aren’t safe places to live, right? The only trick is that you’ve
got to identify the best, most worthiest thing that you love most and then
build your house right on top of it and don’t budge from it. And if you should
someday, somehow get vaulted out of your home by either great failure or
great success, then your job is to fight your way back to that home the only
way that has ever been done - by putting your head down and performing with
diligence, and devotion, and respect and reverence, whatever the task is that
love is calling forth from you next.
Find that which is bigger than you. Find that which drives you in your life. For
us, it is the Gospel of the kingdom of Christ. That is so important that
everything else becomes secondary. If you can find that dedication to Christ,
that should be your “home.” When we find ourselves acting out of accordance
with what our home dictates, we have to fight our way back to it.
Great peace is found by living a life of integrity. Being honest, caring and
vulnerable, trying to help others – what a way to live!
What is God’s future remedy for failure due to choice? First,
God will wipe away all of the other excuses so all that is left is
choice.
God will grant full disclosure in the Day of Judgment.
Full Disclosure - this will solve the lack of knowledge failure:
1 Timothy 2:4: (NASB) who desires all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the
truth.
Notice, FIRST all men are saved and THEN they will come to
the knowledge of the truth. Isn’t that backwards? People
always say you learn about the Gospel and then you are
“saved.” This is backwards because it is not talking about
Christians. It is talking about the “everybody else.” They will
be saved – they are given a resurrection and judgment
according to John 5:28,29 (NASB). THEN they will come to a
knowledge of the truth. The Greek word for knowledge here
means “full disclosure.” They will understand everything, clearly. There will
be no way to say, “I didn’t get it.” In dealing with humanity after the
resurrection, God will say a lack of knowledge is no longer an excuse. His
mercy will not allow a lack of knowledge to get in their way.
Complete Accountability - this will solve the immaturity failure:
Matthew 12:34-36: (NASB) 34You brood of vipers, how can you, being evil, speak what is
good? For the mouth speaks out of that which fills the heart. 35The good man brings out of his
good treasure what is good; and the evil man brings out of his evil treasure what is evil. 36But I

tell you that every careless word that people speak, they shall give an accounting for it in the
day of judgment.
Carelessness is often a result of immaturity. Jesus was specifically focusing on
the Pharisees at this point, who were not on a pathway to heaven. They were
on the road to resurrection in the next age, being bought by the sacrifice of
Jesus. He died for even his enemies – the ones who put him on the cross.
You brood of vipers - that would have gotten their attention!
They shall give an accounting for it in the day of judgment - They will be
accountable for their actions.
God will put all of the world in a situation where they will be able to grow up.
Lots of room to learn – this will solve the weakness failure:
Isaiah 35:8: (Leeser) And there shall be a highway and a way, and the holy way, shall it be
called; no unclean one shall pass over it; but it shall be only theirs; the wayfaring man, and
those unacquainted therewith, shall not go astray.
Again, those on this highway are the “everybody else,” not the true Christians.
Conversely, the Christian walk is referred to as straight, difficult and narrow.
This is a large highway. Even if they are not sure of themselves, there will be
plenty of room to learn. God will take away the weakness failures because
they will have time and opportunity to learn.
Once all these other things have gone away, we are left with failure due to
choice.
Full personal responsibility for each person’s decisions and actions - this
leaves only free, educated, experienced and mature choice for man’s
ultimate individual judgment:
Jeremiah 31:29-30: (NASB) 29In those days they will not say again, the fathers have eaten

Psalm 22:27-28: (NASB) 27All the ends of the earth will remember and turn to the LORD,

He rules over the nations.

Do the Fires of Hell Come From God? (Part III) 
Acts 3:23: (NASB) And it will be that every soul that does not heed that 
prophet shall be utterly destroyed from among the people. 
The world is messed up.  If you believe in God, then you most 
likely believe in some sort of ultimate justice system.  The 
question is, what does God’s system of justice consist of – 
what kind of penalty?  For generations, the majority of 
Christianity has believed in a hell of fire and torment as the 
answer to this question. However, there is a mountain of 
biblical evidence to the contrary. Today we will embark on 
Part III of our series that examines this evidence.  We will look 
at some of the really difficult and seemingly contradictory 
Scriptures that talk about the condition of those who were evil in this life.  Do 
they go to hell?  Is there fire and torment in hell? 
“Do the Fires of Hell Come From God (Part I)” on June 7, 2015 examined the 
biblical phrase weeping (or wailing) and gnashing of teeth, with the conclusion 
that its meaning was focusing on deep heartbreaking sorrow and anguish 
coupled with consternation, anger and pain at a GREAT loss.  This reaction 
never applied to any eternal torment or torture – only to the loss of 
opportunity of God’s favor at one time or another. 
“Do the Fires of Hell Come From God (Part II)” on July 26, 2015 examined the 
Greek word Gehenna, meaning the Valley of Hinnom, a word often translated 
as hellfire.  We saw how this Valley was used as a garbage dump where fires 
constantly burned to utterly destroy all therein, and how it symbolized utter 
and disgraceful destruction.  Because of the heinous sins previously committed 
there, God declared it a place of utter destruction, not torture.  Bodies of 
criminals (dead, never live) were thrown in here, denied an honorable burial. 
Today, Part III will examine the word Hades and its Old Testament counterpart 
Sheol, often translated hell.  What does it mean?  How is it used?  Jesus used 
the Old Testament as his foundation for the New Testament, so we will as well. 
In the Old Testament, there is only one word translated hell: 
Sheol:  Strongs #7585 she'owl (sheh-ole') Hades or the world of the dead  
(as if a subterranean retreat), including its accessories and inmates 
 When translated into English, this Hebrew word Sheol is translated: 
• Grave – 31 times 
• Hell – 31 times 
• Pit – 3 times 

When we think of “the grave,” it brings to mind where we respectfully put a 
deceased body.  When we hear the word hell, based on our Christian 
denomination, we could think of several different things.  Some may think of it 
  as a place of eternal torment.   

So, our first problem is the Old Testament uses the exact same word, Sheol, 
but translates into English three different ways with three different English 
 meanings. 
Let’s look at some of the “warnings” using this word:  
Deuteronomy 32:21-23: (KJV) 21They have moved me to jealousy with that which is not 
God; they have provoked me to anger with their vanities: and I will move them to jealousy 
with those, which are not a people; I will provoke them to anger with a foolish nation. (This 
text was quoted and fulfilled in Romans 10:19-21 relating to the Gentiles coming to favor 
thousands of years later.) 22For a fire is kindled in mine anger, and shall burn unto the lowest 
hell <7585>, and shall consume the earth with her increase, and set on fire the foundations of 
the mountains.   
This is figurative language describing the “fire” of God’s anger.

Let me just explain a little bit of why hell is eternal and why it should be and

ultimately means even when there’s a gross injustice against me, it’s a sin

What about the New Testament? 
New Testament Greek word: 
Hades:  Strongs #86 haides (hah'-dace); properly, unseen, i.e. 
 "Hades" or the place (state) of departed souls; KJV-- grave, hell. 
Something buried under the ground is unseen.

He is being sarcastic to prove a point.  This is his reasoning for attempting to

Jesus is teaching several audiences all at once with a series of parables: 
Luke 15:1-3: (NKJV) 1Then all the tax collectors and the sinners drew near to him to hear

Luke 15:3-7: The first Parable of the Lost 
Sheep shows the recovery of mankind from 
their lost state of sin. Jesus gives the 
interpretation of his theme - joy in heaven.  
He tells them this lesson plainly, so they can 
follow his themes as they unfold into lessons 
of plain truth about the development of his 
Father’s kingdom - and condemnation for 
being too proud and egotistical to comply with 
it.  He is talking directly to the Pharisees. 

Luke 15:8-10: The second Parable of the Lost Coin illustrates in its 
big picture the value of the redeemed race of man as a part of the 
symmetry of the ten coins being restored – the lost coin 
symbolizing the race of man and the woman symbolizing the work 
of reconciliation. 

Luke 15:11-32: The third Parable of the Prodigal 
Son shows the two classes of Israel – the 
Pharisees represented in the older brother and 
the sinners and publicans represented in the 
younger one.  (Incidentally, all of these 
classes of people were in front of Jesus 
while he was telling these parables!)  
This story reveals the attitudes of both 
classes and the grace of God in 
accepting repentance. 
Luke 16:1-15: The fourth Parable of the 
Unjust Steward frontally attacked the 
selfish and compromising spirit the 
Pharisees displayed, showing their 
hypocrisy and godlessness. 
Jesus is dealing with a wide audience from publicans and sinners to tax 
collectors, scribes and Pharisees. 

Now, The fifth Parable of the Rich Man and 
Lazarus, a lesson in reversal:  The story starts 
with the rich man being favored and the beggar 
out of favor.  
Luke 16:19-21: (KJV) 19There was a certain rich man, 
which was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared

• Fared sumptuously every day – he 
enjoyed but did not appreciate his 
blessings 
20And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, which was laid at his gate, full of sores, 21And

• Lazarus - represented the Gentiles – the “everybody else” outside of the

Torments: Strongs #931 basanos (bas'-an-os); a touchstone 
Greek English Lexicon: a touchstone, which is a black siliceous stone used to test the purity of 
gold or silver by the color of the streak produced on it by rubbing it with metal  
by which one is forced to divulge the truth 

(Source: Wikipedia, “Metallurgical assay”)  The age-old 
touchstone method is particularly suited to the testing 
of very valuable pieces, for which sampling by 
destructive means, such as scraping, cutting or drilling 
is unacceptable. A rubbing of the item is made on a 
special stone, treated with acids and the resulting 
color compared to references. Red radiolarian chert or 
black siliceous slate were used to view the resultant 
treated streak of the sample. Differences in precious 
metal content as small as 10 to 20 parts per thousand 
can often be established with confidence by the test. It 
is not indicated for use with white gold, for example, 
since the color variation among white gold alloys is almost imperceptible. 
The only other time this word is used:

Location and description, Duat - The Ancient Egyptian Underworld, Experience 
Ancient Egypt 
• 
The ancient Egyptian religion was not standardized, and the different texts 
that explained different beliefs and practices were not considered absolute.  
They mixed and changed.  Some were evolutions of older ones, and some just 
went in and out of popularity.  And so, it 
was the same with the concept of the 
underworld.  But for the sake of 
simplicity, let’s take a look at the most 
prevalent belief about Duat.  In ancient 
Egyptian cosmology, the earth was 
thought to be flat and oval-shaped and 
surrounded by oceans.  Underneath it lay 
the vast expanse of the underworld, with 
the primordial waters of Nun running 
through it.  Nun was the state of chaos 
that existed before creation.  The 
landscape of Duat was similar to that of 
earth’s but with a more malevolent 
flavor.  There were trees and mountains 
and rivers, but also lakes of fires, dark 
caverns, evil spirits and serpents.  The 
Papyrus of Ani has some very interesting 
 depictions of it. 

These writings are dated somewhere during the 18th Dynasty of Egypt which 
began when Moses was a young man, before he brought Israel out of Egypt.  
Such beliefs were probably in existence long before this. 

How much of the Egyptian beliefs did the Israelites accept?  We do not know, 
but we know they did build a golden calf (Exodus 32) – where would they have 
gotten that idea?  Not from God.  They would have been surrounded by the 
well-defined Egyptian thought process of an underworld. 
How did God specifically teach His people the truths  
of life and death when surrounded by paganism?   

Once this question is answered, it will give us a real understanding of how to 
read Scripture on these issues.  Let’s start by remembering that God delivered 
Israel from Egypt through ten plagues.  Interestingly, these plagues were 
directed at many of the gods of Egypt.  It seems that God was showing His 
people that HE was God and these other things were mere idolatry. 
Eternal and fiery, HELL: The Teaching of the Church Affirms the Existence of Hell 
and its Eternity, Father J. Corapi  
• 
Every now and then some well-meaning theologian, as he gets older, comes up 
with the conclusion that hell isn’t eternal, that God could never do that.  This 
is doctrinal:  there is a hell, and it’s forever.  Immediately after death, the 
souls of those who die in a state of mortal sin descend into hell, where they 
suffer the punishments of hell - eternal fire.  The chief punishment of hell is 
eternal separation from God, in whom alone man can possess the life and 
happiness for which he was created and for which he longs.   
(Source: The Hell of Ancient Egypt by John Watson, touregypt.net, continued) The concept of 
hell in the ancient Egyptian religion is very similar to those of our modern religions.  Those who 
were judged unfavorably faced a very similar fate to our modern concept of hell, and perhaps 
even more specifically to the more Middle Age concept of it as a specific region beneath the 
earth.  For the damned, the entire, uncontrollable rage of the deity was directed against those 
who were condemned through their evils.  They were tortured in every imaginable way and 
"destroyed", thus being consigned to nonexistence.  They were deprived of their sense organs, 
were required to walk on their heads and eat their own excrement.  They were burned in ovens 
and cauldrons and were forced to swim in their own blood, which Shezmu, the god of the wine 
press, squeezed out of them.

SECTION I: DESCRIPTION OF THE HEATHEN HELL:  Among the ancient pagans, the belief in a hell 
of some sort was very general, if not universal.  It was known by various names, as Orcus, 
Erebus, Tartarus, and Infernus or Inferna, whence our expression "infernal regions," etc.  The 
views current respecting it were different at different periods, and among different nations, 
according to the degree of civilization and the genius of the people.  What I shall offer on this 
point will have respect mostly to the Romans, Greeks and Egyptians. 
Its location: It was supposed to be as far below the earth (or as deep down in it), as the 
heavens are above it, Hesiod, the Greek poet, who lived 850 BC, (around the time of Elijah) is 
very precise in his statement, and says a mass of iron would be nine days falling from heaven to 
earth, and nine more in falling from earth to hell.  So say also Apollodorus, Virgil and others. 
Observations: 
• God never warned Adam of sin leading to torment – the consequence was 
simply death. 
• Egyptian culture (and others) before Moses’ time clearly had graphic 
written descriptions of a “netherworld.”  
• At its beginning, Jewish culture had no such thing – they only had death 
and burial underground in Sheol. 
• God vividly demonstrated the difference between Himself and the gods 
of Egypt, especially in His deliverance plagues. 
• God NEVER warned Israel of some future torture as a result of 
disobedience. 
• All of the penalties of God’s Law to Israel were tribulations IN THIS LIFE.  
Not one word about hell! 
Did God add to or change what He told Israel about  
life and death as time went on? 
Our last historical reference was to a Greek poet who lived around 850 BC.  
This moves us forward in time over 600 years from the previous references.  
While Israel did not have much to do with Greek culture, they were by this 
time steeped in the mire of Canaanite culture and fighting what seemed to be 
a never-ending battle against idolatry.   
This is a key to understanding biblical truth.  What was Israel fighting against?  
How did God support them in that fight?  Did they fall?  Did they stand?  What 
did the prophets say?  What were the consequences?  We must ask all of these 
questions (and more!) if we want to find biblical truth. 
To just take a verse out of context and assume it means one thing is not 
correct.  Put history and biblical truth next to each other both inside and 
outside of Judaism.

While Greeks were dropping iron anvils down to the netherworld, Elijah was 
challenging the ascendency of Baal in Israel at the hands of Ahab and Jezebel. 
(Source:  gotquestions.org) Who was Baal?  According to Canaanite mythology, Baal was the 
son of El, the chief god, and Asherah, the goddess of the sea.  Baal was considered the most 
powerful of all gods, eclipsing El, who was seen as rather weak and ineffective.  In various 
battles Baal defeated Yamm, the god of the sea, and Mot, the god of death and the 
underworld.  Baal’s sisters/consorts were Ashtoreth, a fertility goddess associated with the 
stars, and Anath, a goddess of love and war.  The Canaanites worshiped Baal as the sun god and 
as the storm god — he is usually depicted holding a lightning bolt — who defeated enemies and 
produced crops. 
How did God address the Baal issue? 
• There was no rain for several years.  Baal was a storm god,  
yet they had no rain, showing Baal’s weakness. 
• Rain only came again when Elijah said it would, showing 
God’s ascendancy.  
• God sent fire down from heaven to consume Elijah’s sacrifice 
when Baal, the lightning bolt bearer, could do nothing, showing 
God’s miraculous and unmatched power. 
God continued to address other gods by showing His power in areas 
where they claimed power.   
Their belief system was different than all people around them.  We believe this 
belief in torment that was in all of these pagan worlds, Canaanites included - 
had an “underworld” belief as well.  Israel did not have such a belief. 

(Source: “The Origin and History of the Doctrine of Endless Punishment” by Thomas B. Thayer, 
New and enlarged edition. Boston: Universalist Publishing House. 1881.) 
SECTION II: THE HEATHEN INVENTED THE DOCTRINE OF ENDLESS PUNISHMENT - SHOWN BY 
THEIR OWN CONFESSIONS.  …all the early lawgivers claim to have had communications with the 
gods, who aided them in the preparation of their codes.  Zoroaster claimed to have received 
his laws from a divine source; Lycurgus obtained his from Apollo, Minos of Crete from Jupiter, 
Numa of Rome from Egeria, Zaleucus from Minerva, etc.  The object of this sacred fraud was to 
impress the minds of the multitude with religious awe and command a more ready obedience 
on their part. 
Pagan history claimed to receive beliefs from divine sources, which made the 
people afraid and submissive.  Fear drives obedience.  Zoroastrianism arose in 
the eastern region of the ancient Persian Empire, when the religious 
philosopher Zoroaster simplified the pantheon of early Iranian gods into two 
opposing forces, in the 7th century BCE, around the time of Jeremiah.

Is Gratitude Your Attitude?
Hebrews 13:15: (NASB) Through Him then, let us continually offer
up a sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of
lips that give thanks to His name.
Here is a question: what do the Fourth of July and
Thanksgiving have in common? The most obvious answer is
that these two celebrations are uniquely American in that
their very founding were undeniably linked to the founding
of the United States. The less obvious answer is that these
two holidays were also founded in humble recognition of
God Almighty.
Just read the first and last parts of the
Declaration of Independence and the first Declaration for
Thanksgiving of the United States, and you will see that God
was first and foremost. Here we are about 240 years later,
and God is no longer first, and He certainly is no longer “for
most.” As we approach the Thanksgiving holiday, what can
we do to relight our own fire of gratitude towards God and towards one another?
Let us start by talking about it.
This week we will focus on several Profiles of Gratitude. But first, we want to
find out what gratitude can do for us.
What good is gratitude, Robert Emmons, Greater Good Science Center
•
Number 1: It allows us to celebrate the present, a magnification of positive
emotions. We know from research by emotion scientists that positive
emotions wear off quickly. Our emotional systems like newness. They like
novelty; they like change. We adapt to positive life circumstances so that the
new car, the new spouse, the new house, the new whatever is not so new after
a short period of time. We adapt to it. Gratitude involves the appreciation of
the value of something, and so when we appreciate the value of it we are less
likely to depreciate the value, which is to lose value; therefore we extract
more benefits.
•
Number 2: Gratitude blocks negative emotions, toxic emotions which can
destroy our happiness, subjective well-being, optimal functioning, particularly
in the domain of envy, resentment, regret, even depression. There is new
evidence coming out showing that gratitude is effective in the prevention,
reduces the episodes of depression, reduces the duration, and makes future
episodes less likely. You cannot be envious and grateful at the same time.
Try it, you can’t. They’re incompatible feelings. You can’t resent someone
for having something that they have that you don’t if you are grateful. Those
are very different ways of being in the world.
Gratitude can have an enormous impact in our lives.
