We went to our resident expert, friend and Professor of Microbiology at 
Marshall University, Dr. Wendy Trzyna, to explain this relatively new study of 
epigenetics and how it might influence what people call “generational curses.”  
(We will talk further on this subject in Part II of this series).  We first asked her 
to explain what this is all about: 
What is epigenetics, Dr. Wendy 
• 
Every one of us is defined by our genomes, which is essentially the collection 
of genes we’ve inherited from our parents.  However, our traits and 
characteristics are also influenced by the environment and our experiences, 
which is the component we typically refer to as “nurture.”  It is generally 
accepted that nature and nurture both contribute to making us who we are.  
Although the human genome was sequenced nearly two decades ago, there is 
still much to be learned about exactly how much our genes are responsible for 
certain behaviors and characteristics and how much is determined by the 
environment, and also how these components work together.  The exciting 
field of epigenetics investigates how the environment can influence or change 
patterns of gene expression in our cells.  Epigenetic patterns can affect many 
things like our behaviors, responses and susceptibility to various diseases. 
Unlike genetic changes, epigenetic changes are reversible and do not change 
your DNA sequences, but rather how and when a DNA sequence is read.  
Epigenetic changes are chemical markers that are added to specific sites along 
the genome, and what chemical is added and where determines the effect 
that occurs.  Epigenetic changes have been linked to all sorts of issues like 
metabolic diseases, cancers, Alzheimer’s, schizophrenia and PTSD.  
These epigenetic modifications switch specific genes on and off according to 
environmental and other triggers – although the DNA sequence itself does not 
change, those changed markers that sit on top of the DNA can be passed down 
through generations. 
There is a hidden world of biological information within each of us.  This helps 
us understand the uniqueness we all have - and therefore the unique challenges 
we each face. 
The Apostle Paul hinted at this uniqueness: 
1 Corinthians 2:11-12: (Weymouth) 11For, among human beings, who knows a man's 
inner thoughts except the man's own spirit within him? In the same way, also, only God's spirit 
is acquainted with God's inner thoughts. 12But we have not received the spirit of the world, 
but the spirit which comes forth from God, that we may know the blessings that have been so 
freely given to us by God. 
When we read these verses in light of epigenetics, which says each of us has 
chemical markers on our DNA causing a physiological switch on or off, it seems 
as though the Apostle Paul had insight that each of us is entirely unique in our 
thinking.  Paul says we cannot know another man’s inner thoughts because we 
are each wired to react differently.  There is physiological proof of this!  For 
someone afraid of generational curses, this information can help us hold on to 
hope.    
We know parents pass on their DNA to their children, but can they also pass on 
 these chemical markers that change how our DNA is read?   

      Are epigenetic changes heritable, Dr. Wendy 
• 
Now the interesting question is whether or not these epigenetic changes can 
be passed on to one’s offspring.  In other words, if you acquire a metabolic 
disease through environmental factors, will that tendency be passed on to 
your children or even your grandchildren?  Until recently, we thought the 
answer was no.  In fact, the data traditionally shows that in mammals the 
slate is essentially wiped clean of any epigenetic modifications, and the 
offspring begins anew.  However, a small number of studies have shown that 
this reprogramming did not always occur completely, leaving a few 
modifications behind, and thus leaving open the possibility for 
transgenerational inheritance related especially to things like metabolic 
disorders such as diabetes and obesity.  The studies also showed that when 
these environmentally-induced disorders were prevalent in fathers, the 
offspring had an increased risk, or tendency, for developing these conditions 
as well. 
Seeing these epigenetic markers pass from generation to generation is 
fascinating.  This is not the gene itself; this is a chemical marker that turns the 
gene on and off.  It was thought that children receiving their parents’ genes 
would not inherit the markers, but new studies indicate this can happen.   
Although he was not referring to epigenetics, the Apostle Paul showed us 
how to apply encouragement to the paradox of our fleshly being: 
Romans 7:21-25: (NASB) 21I find then the principle that evil is present in me, the one who 
wants to do good. 22For I joyfully concur with the law of God in the inner man, 23but I see a 
different law in the members of my body, waging war against the law of my mind and making 
me a prisoner of the law of sin which is in my members. 24Wretched man that I am! Who will 
set me free from the body of this death? 25Thanks be to God through Jesus Christ our Lord! So 
then, on the one hand I myself with my mind am serving the law of God, but on the other, 
with my flesh the law of sin. 
Paul acknowledged the weaknesses and inclinations he was wired for.   
They were always with him, but he did not have to follow these tendencies!  
He could choose not to.  He had the inner struggle but could rise to the level of 
Christlikeness, even if his “wiring” was tugging him in the other direction.   
As Christians, we can be encouraged when overcoming the irrational fears of 
many things, including curses, by accepting the duality of our physical being 
striving for a spiritual life. 
What if Satan, one of the highest of God’s 
creations back in the beginning of time, knew 
about DNA and these epigenetic markers 
influenced by experiences?  What if he knew 
he could push certain experiences that could 
place markers on person’s DNA, bending them toward sin or towards feeling 
they were being cursed?  Satan, a psychopath, wants to do harm to all of God’s 
creation.  He boasted he would be like the Most High in Isaiah 14:14.  In his sick 
way, he can manipulate, guide, direct and control people - even brainwash 
them.  In revenge, he wants to destroy or pervert what God loves. 

     Mouse study, Dr. Wendy  
• 
In a study carried out in mice, the mice were subjected to behavioral 
conditioning where they were exposed to a specific scent and then 
administered an electric shock.  Over time the mice associated the scent with 
the trauma, and eventually just the scent alone would trigger the trauma 
response.  Their offspring, as well as the next generation, also demonstrated a 
fear of the smell, even though they had never been exposed to the scent 
before or conditioned to react in that manner.  This study suggests that the 
scent response was passed on to the next generation.  Even physical changes in 
their brains were observed.  Similar tendencies have been described in studies 
of children of Holocaust survivors and more recently, babies born to women 
who experienced trauma from the World Trade 
Center attacks of 9/11.  In the latter case, lower 
levels of cortisol were observed in both the 
mothers and their offspring, attributed to PTSD 
(Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder) during gestation.  
This resulted in children who developed 
hypertension, insulin resistance and depression. 
Scientists found that all three generations of mice had a higher-than-average 
number of olfactory receptors to detect the odor.  It appears the mice 
inherited the trauma of their ancestors!  Human studies have suggested similar 
conclusions.   
These generations of mice feared a scent they never smelled before.  It was 
expected that only those who had been conditioned to fear the smell would 
react.  
Even though our biology might be programmed this way, we are not required to 
give in to it.  We are looking at the propensity to feel like we are cursed or our 
family is cursed and wanting to break the curse.  We need to break the thinking 
that feeds the superstition.  We want to examine the many aspects that can 
lead to this fear.   
The Apostle Paul prepares us for such challenges by displaying his own clear 
spiritual focus: 
Philippians 4:12-13: (NASB) 12I know how to get along with humble means, and I also know 
how to live in prosperity; in any and every circumstance I have learned the secret of being 
filled and going hungry, both of having abundance and suffering need. 13I can do all things 
through him who strengthens me. 
The Apostle Paul tells us that whatever circumstance came his way, he could 
manage because he had Christ as his anchor.  We can also tap into this spiritual 
focus no matter how our chemical wiring afflicts us.  It may not be easy, but 
we have this same heavenly help available to us.  As Christians, we are 
compelled to fulfill the calling of our discipleship and not give in to what we 
naturally crave.    
Dr. Wendy shared an additional study looking at epigenetic 
markers in patients with military PTSD.  The epigenetic 
modification actually changed as a result of successful 
 treatment.   

Quoting from its summary, “This study showed a clear link between a 
psychological or behavioral modification and a detectable biological change.”  
They were able to remove the epigenetic marker that triggered the PTSD 
symptoms.  In other words, the chemical sitting on the person’s DNA could be 
removed or changed by therapy.  What hope this gives for all of us in changing 
 our reactions and fears to certain stressors! 
Please see the Bonus Material for the professional references Dr. Wendy 
provides. 
My wife, Tricia, went through PTSD.  Her life fell apart before both our eyes.  
She received treatment, but it was difficult as I watched her struggle and 
recovery.  Seeing her now versus then is like night and day.  Something 
changed during that treatment.  The description of epigenetic modifications 
really does fit her experience.  
We know that if we are faithful in our Christian walk, we will be given the job 
of rehabilitating mankind in God’s kingdom.  By realizing we all have these 
markers, we can help others by empathizing and showing how God helped us 
overcome our own tendencies. 
Where are you finding strength?  
All the epigenetics research is enlightening and helps us focus in on separating 
curse facts from curse fiction. 
How far into Christianity has the mentality of generational 
 or individual curses come?  Should we be scared?   
This is a big question, and unfortunately the answer can be depressing.  As with 
any other aspect of life, there are those who claim the name of Christ and use 
it for personal gain.  The superstition of curses is evident everywhere we look. 
Unfortunately, the business of removing these curses is also alive and well. 
This is not limited to your local fake psychic on the corner, although they have 
scammed people out of millions of dollars promising to remove curses.  If you 
do not fall for that, perhaps you will be taken in by popular churches who are 
happy to sell you books and courses on how to remove curses to give you all 
you want in life. 

The BUSINESS of curse removal outside of Christianity: 
(Source: westsidetoday.com, Breakfast Food to Remove Curses? March 10, 2020) According to 
the Los Angeles Police Department: “These types of scams are more common than one may 
think and target emotionally, physically and spiritually vulnerable victims.  The scams often 
involve eggs and/or bananas to determine the extent of a curse, and a promise to return any 
money or valuables the victim may provide the suspect. 
Victims are often reluctant to report these incidents out of embarrassment and fear of being 
ostracized and scorned by their friends and family.”  
These scams work because people are too embarrassed to admit they were 
taken in by them.  This is widespread.  There are many reports detailing scams 
to get rid of curses.  Most of the belief in curses is based on superstition.  
The BUSINESS of curse removal from within Christianity: 
Some “Prosperity Gospel” preachers say that while we know God as our Father, 
He is also the Judge in the Courts of Heaven, which coincidentally operates like 
our modern legal system.  The theology is based on the idea that God gave 
Adam legal authority over earth.  When Adam sinned, he lost that authority to 
Satan.  They say God cannot legally take action unless we somehow 
take that authority from Satan and give it back to God.  Supposedly, 
this is why so many prayers go unanswered because we first have to 
obtain “legal verdicts from heaven.”  Basically, God is UNABLE to bless 
us unless we do something to take the authority from Satan. 
(Source:  https://www.destinyimage.com/blog/2016/08/05/robert-henderson-breaking-curses-
in-the-courts-of-heaven blog by Robert Henderson) One of the functions of the heavenly Courts 
is to “unlock our destinies by dissolving curses against us that are denying and delaying our 
futures.”  Another crucial issue to dissolving curses is to recognize they can operate among a 
New Testament people…  
We have been saying all along that most of this is superstition.  Here you have 
a Christian saying how we need to dissolve these generational curses and “they 
can operate among New Testament people…”  We are a “New Testament 
people,” and he is saying these curses are alive and well today.  This is a 
completely opposite viewpoint to ours.  To continue… 
When Jesus declared, “It is finished” on the cross, he was declaring that every legal 
requirement had been met for the reconciliation and reclaiming of all things back to God.   
The problem is that it is one thing for a legal verdict to be rendered and another for the 
execution of it to take place.  When a judge sits on a bench and renders a verdict, he doesn’t 
then come down from that bench and enforce it.  There are others who must take the legal 
rendering of the judge and execute it into place until it has practical and functional 
ramifications.  The holy spirit came to empower us to be the officers of the court to execute 
into place that judgment. 
He is taking the beauty of the ransom price of Jesus with its promise of 
reconciliation as a result of that ransom and trying to apply it to everyday life 
to remove curses!  This is NOT what the ransom is about.  The reconciliation 
Jesus will accomplish will bring the world of mankind back to God – not what 
some see in their minds now in relation to curses.  He is completely upending 
the message, the main point of the gospel. 

(Source:  https://dougaddison.com/2018/03/6-types-of-courts-in-the-courts-of-heaven)  
The Courts of Heaven operate similar to the legal system we see on earth.  Because of all the 
injustices happening in the world, God is releasing new revelation about gaining justice through 
the Courts of Heaven.  The Cross of Christ is our verdict but there are times we need to 
enforce this by entering into the justice system of God. We operate in the Courts of Heaven 
through prayer and an intimate relationship with the Lord. 
In researching this topic, we saw scriptures being grossly misrepresented in 
order to support this “new revelation.”   
Here is the first of just two examples: 
Matthew 5:25: (KJV) Agree with thine adversary quickly, whiles thou art in 
the way with him; lest at any time the adversary deliver thee to the judge, 
and the judge deliver thee to the officer, and thou be cast into prison. 
Jesus is talking here about agreeing with your adversary before 
going to court so that you will have an easier verdict.  The Courts 
of Heaven teaching use this verse to say we need to agree with 
Satan about the sins we have committed.  This is not even 
remotely close to what Jesus meant in this verse!  We are NOT to 
have conversations with Satan. 
Even worse is the perversion of the next text: 
Psalms 40:7-8: (KJV) 7Then said I, Lo, I come: in the volume (scroll) of the book it is 
written of me, 8I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.   
They interpret the scroll as a legal document requiring us to 
find legal representation.  But these verses are about Jesus, not 
us!  It is a complete misrepresentation of these beautiful 
scriptures.  
We know this by seeing where it is quoted in Hebrews: 
Hebrews 10:7,9,10,12: (KJV) 7Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is 
written of me,) to do thy will, O God. 9Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He 
taketh away the first, that He may establish the second. 10By the which will we are sanctified 
through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all. 12But this man, after he had 
offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God;  
This theology misrepresents many scriptures, creating a scenario about a 
fictitious court in heaven.  This court does not exist.  They claim it will remove 
curses and give you all you want and deserve in this life, including justice when 
it is not found in earthly courts.  Please do not go down this road! 
We wanted to play a short audio clip to describe how this all works, but it is

 All of this “new revelation” with NO scriptural basis?  Let’s refocus. 
What should we believe if we have a fear of curses? 
1 Peter 5:6-8: (NASB) 6Therefore humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God, that

So, are curses real?  We believe some are, and Satan is behind them.  
Did God curse people in the Bible?  Yes, but we have to be careful with the 
word “curse,” as we will explain.  There definitely are curses in the Bible, and 
we will focus on these in Parts II and III.   

In this episode, we are looking at the superstitions which we have inside of us 
that may make us susceptible to these things. 

This is Satan’s game, and he plays it well! 

Let’s begin to put our biblical understanding of curses in order: 
Genesis 3:14,16-17: (NASB) 14The LORD God said to the serpent, Because you have done 
this, cursed <779> are you more than all cattle, and more than every beast of the field; on 
your belly you will go, and dust you will eat all the days of your life; 16to the woman He said, I 
will greatly multiply your pain in childbirth, in pain you will bring forth children; yet your  
desire will be for your husband, and he will rule over you. 17Then to Adam He said, Because 
you have listened to the voice of your wife, and have eaten from the tree about which I 
commanded you, saying, You shall not eat from it; cursed <779> is the ground because of 
you; in toil you will eat of it all the days of your life.  
Curse:  Strongs #779 'arar; to execrate 

God cursed Satan (who was manifesting himself in 
the form of a serpent), and God also cursed the 
ground because of Adam’s disobedience. 
Why didn’t God “curse” Eve?   
He did not “curse” Adam either!  Wait a minute…we often speak about Adam 
and Eve being under the curse of sin.  However, in light of today’s discussion 
and the world’s definition of “curse” - meaning wishing harm to someone -  
we want to clarify:   
For Adam and Eve, being under the curse of sin meant facing the severe 
consequences of their sinful actions.  God did NOT want them to be harmed; 
He DID want them to learn!  In today’s definition, cursing someone means you 
wish harm on someone; God did not do that. 
When God placed these curses, He was expressing “execration,” a loathing for 
that which He cursed.  For Satan, this meant he would be banished out of the 
light of God’s power and presence but would be allowed to exist with the 
limited power God would allow him to wield.   
In this great universe, any being existing outside of the light and influence of 
God is inherently evil, and therefore will act against God’s will.  God sees any 
being outside of His light as treasonous, and therefore He sees it with loathing.   
God loathes Satan’s ways because he is a treasonous being - a traitor, trying to 
undo the goodness, mercy, power and benevolence of God.  This holds true for 
the fallen angels that followed Satan before the Flood as well. 
When God cursed the ground for Adam’s sake, He ceased to develop the earth’s 
productivity to the level of the Garden of Eden.  The ground was unfinished - 
it had not been brought to perfection like the Garden of Eden.  It would grow 
things haphazardly, without the refinements from God’s hand to maximize its 
efficiency.  Adam’s consequence was to manage the earth without the hand of 

God.  The ground was not finished; it was outside of God’s light.  The ground 
was cursed so that man could learn.  When God cursed the ground, 
it was not that He wished to cause evil, but that He planned consequences for 
the sake of learning. 
The English word “curse” is very imprecise.  In the rest of this three-part 
series, we are going to see that the Old Testament Hebrew language has 14 
different words for our one English word “curse,” and the New Testament 
Greek has nine, all with slightly different shades of meaning.  
This is like the word “love” in the New Testament.  Storge, philia and agape all 
have different shades of meaning and come in different forms, but all are 
translated “love” in the Bible.
